nodes.response: When objects are grouped in tens, use deliberate errors and discussion to draw attention to the total number of ones represented by the number, so children are familiar with recognising both the extra ones and the total number of ones in a number.

nodes.misconception: Recording ten tenths as 0.10 rather than 1 or 1.0
nodes.response: Be sure to address this regularly with pupils whilst counting. Demonstrate the regrouping using place value counters to help.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle with balance due to weak core muscles. Pupils may always want to use the same apparatus in the same area.
nodes.response: Add some core strengthening exercises into the warm up and emphasise the importance of core strength in all activities. Encourage pupils to use a range of apparatus throughout the lesson to develop their confidence.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that a partner balance is a counter balance.  Pupils may struggle with counter balance due to unequal weight distribution. Pupils may struggle to trust their partner.
nodes.response: Show the difference between a partner balance and a counter balance. Pupils practice positions individually and work together to adjust the balance equally. Incorporate activities that require working together and communication to build trust.

nodes.misconception: One pupil pulls harder or doesn’t pull enough, leading to an imbalance and collapse of the position. Pupils do not have a secure grip with one another
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to communicate with their partners pulling gently at first, then increase force gradually to find the balance point. Encourage pupils to grip using wrists as an alternative to hands.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that tackling a raider individually is the only option.
nodes.response: In Kabaddi, Raiders have 30 seconds to make the raid and get back across the half way line. As a result, if the defense hold up the raider until their time runs out, it is an unsuccessful raid and the raider doesn't score.

nodes.misconception: All tally marks should look the same in a straight line.
nodes.response: Every fifth mark in a tally chart should be placed diagonally across a group of four. We do this to make it easier to count the total.

nodes.misconception: Mistakes when counting in ones. Children may not be able to visualise numbers to see which is more/greater than, less than or equal to.
nodes.response: Children should continue to practise counting forwards and backwards from a given number to increase confidence of counting within 100. Use number lines or one hundred squares to help children visualise numbers and support comparison.

nodes.misconception: Knowing the number before when counting backwards.
nodes.response: Giving 2 or 3 numbers to establish a pattern then reducing to 2 and then just the given number.

nodes.misconception: Unnecessarily re-counting all objects in a group rather than counting on from an existing amount.
nodes.response: Repeat the key sentence, 'we start our count at ___, and we count ___'.

nodes.misconception: Failing to match one count to one action.
nodes.response: Slow the counting and make the action and count very deliberately at the same time so pupils can imitate the modelling.

nodes.misconception: Confusion between teen and decade numbers, e.g. 19 and 90, leading to errors in counting 80, 90, 20
nodes.response: Regular identification and discussion of common errors with opportunities to correct them within this lesson can be replicated beyond it.

nodes.misconception: May confuse decade number names with teen numbers e.g. thirteen, thirty.
nodes.response: Regular identification and discussion of common errors with opportunities to correct them within this lesson can be replicated beyond it.

nodes.misconception: Saying number names out of order or missing a number name in the sequence.
nodes.response: Repeat the number names in the correct order, emphasising the correction made.

nodes.misconception: Children miss out numbers when skip counting.
nodes.response: Children could have resources like number lines to refer to when counting. These can be removed once children become more confident.

nodes.misconception: Missing out an object or counting one twice. Recounting without concluding how many there are.
nodes.response: Encourage using one finger to move and count each object. From the third learning cycle, repeat 'there are ___ [noun]' following a count.

nodes.misconception: Missing out numbers in the count or not being able to start the count if not at 1.
nodes.response: Give a three number count in to establish a pattern before asking children to join in so 7, 8, 9 given before the children say 10.

nodes.misconception: Confusion when counting select rows on a one hundred square, e.g. children may not use the end of the number (the ones) to help them count accurately, or may say the row ending in 40 is the 'forties'.
nodes.response: Label 'decades' throughout the lesson, and model errors in counting within these so that children get used to hearing when the count doesn't sound right.

nodes.misconception: Missing out numbers in the teens especially when counting backwards.
nodes.response: Repeat the count and stress the missing numbers.

nodes.misconception: The sound-symbol correspondences [ai] and [é/er/ez] sound the same in French.
nodes.response: The letters 'ai/ay' are the same as the SSC [é/er/ez] in French but [ai] is pronounced as in 'vrai' with slightly more relaxed lips than 'ai/ay' in English.

nodes.misconception: The Arctic region is uninhabited.
nodes.response: Approximately 4 million people live in the Arctic region.

nodes.misconception: There is one way of saying 'you' in French.
nodes.response: There are in fact two ways of saying 'you' in French: 'tu' and 'vous'. We use 'tu' when talking to one person and 'vous' when talking to more than one person.

nodes.misconception: Coventry Cathedral only worked for reconciliation in Coventry after the bombing.
nodes.response: Coventry Cathedral seeks reconciliation and peace around the world.

nodes.misconception: Cracking is the same as fractional distillation.
nodes.response: Fractional distillation separates hydrocarbons based on their boiling points. Cracking alters the molecular formula of compounds.

nodes.misconception: In the conclusion of your speech, you should introduce one final point that helps to persuade any audience members who haven't been convinced throughout your speech.
nodes.response: Your conclusion isn't really the place to introduce new ideas as it will be tricky for you to fully develop them before you finish speaking. Instead, use the conclusion to summarise your key ideas and reinforce your central message.

nodes.misconception: That planning is a pointless endeavour.
nodes.response: Planning is a really important aspect of any writing task as it makes the process easier and allows you to organise your thoughts.

nodes.misconception: Refuting counter-arguments is enough to create an impact.
nodes.response: Although it is good practice to refute counter-arguments, we can also use language devices when we do so to make them even more powerful.

nodes.misconception: It doesn't matter how you end a story - people will have the same emotional reaction.
nodes.response: The way that you end a story drastically impacts the lasting emotional impression and how a reader interprets the story.

nodes.misconception: The most important part of dialogue is what is inside the speech marks.
nodes.response: What is said through dialogue is really important, but it's also crucial to consider how that dialogue is to be said. Careful selection of verbs and adverbs give the reader a crucial insight into how dialogue should be read.

nodes.misconception: Lists cannot add sophistication to your writing.
nodes.response: Varying the way we write lists can make our writing more sophisticated.

nodes.misconception: Malevolent characters are always obviously and outwardly evil characters.
nodes.response: Ask pupils whether they can think of any characters from literature where their malevolence is implied or not explicitly stated at first. These characters are often dangerously deceptive.

nodes.misconception: That prepositions aren't an important focal point for descriptive writing.
nodes.response: Not only do prepositions indicate the relationship between words, but they also influence our perception of people based on their body language and positioning in a scene.

nodes.misconception: You should use exclamative sentences all the way through your writing to show tension.
nodes.response: It can be more effective to begin with declarative sentences and progress to exclamative sentences to show the rising tension.

nodes.misconception: Students might confuse isometric drawing with oblique drawing.
nodes.response: Use side by side comparisons to allow students to see the distinct differences.

nodes.misconception: Some pupils may think they can only use scissors to cut paper.
nodes.response: Model tearing and cutting and explain to pupils that choice between the two is important. Tearing makes soft textures like grass or clouds. Cutting makes sharp edges for shapes like windows. Think about which works best for your design.

nodes.misconception: Chalk pastels only come in black and white.
nodes.response: Chalk pastels come in black and white, but they also come in a wide range of bright and vibrant colours.

nodes.misconception: Concrete poems are drawings decorated with words.
nodes.response: Concrete poems integrate text with a shape to convey meaning. They are not merely drawings decorated with words.

nodes.misconception: Africa is one country.
nodes.response: Africa is a continent made up of many different countries and cultures, past and present. Different maps from different times can show this.

nodes.misconception: All kaleidoscope patterns are circular.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that while many have a circular appearance, kaleidoscope patterns can also be based on squares, triangles, and other geometric grids.

nodes.misconception: Artists have group critiques to just suggest ways to make an artwork better.
nodes.response: Group critiques can be useful for an artist to get new ideas or suggestions, but are also useful for other artists to hear the reasons behind the artist's choices.

nodes.misconception: The rolling pin does not have to rest on the guide sticks to ensure an even consistency of clay.
nodes.response: Remind children that the rolling pin should rest on both of the guide sticks.

nodes.misconception: Clay cannot be worked with unless it is very wet.
nodes.response: Clay can be worked with when it is leather hard. This means it has dried out slightly, so it can be stronger to work with.

nodes.misconception: A maquette is a finished sculpture, not a model for planning a design.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that building a maquette is an opportunity to test different elements of their design, allowing them to identify areas for improvement. A maquette does not need to be perfect as its purpose is to resolve issues before the final design.

nodes.misconception: Once an artwork is finished, artists should never change or improve it.
nodes.response: Remind children that looking at your work and finding ways you could improve it is an important part of being an artist.

nodes.misconception: Backgrounds in artworks are not as important as the images within an artwork.
nodes.response: Remind children that backgrounds to artworks can make an image more interesting, or tell us more about the images within an artwork. They can also make an artwork look more three-dimensional.

nodes.misconception: Vector drawings and paint program drawings are the same.
nodes.response: Vector drawings are made out of shapes, paint program drawings are more about line drawing.

nodes.misconception: Children can have difficulty creating problems because they cannot process the amount of information needed and organise their thinking in the way necessary to know how to start.
nodes.response: Give criteria, such as the context, the numbers involved, an equation to represent, or a given structure of addition or subtraction to help focus and structure their thoughts.

nodes.misconception: Some children may not relate the size of the number added/subtracted to the number at the end of the story.
nodes.response: Encourage children to predict how the number at the end of the story will change when the number added/subtracted is increased or decreased.

nodes.misconception: All papers have the same texture.
nodes.response: Remind children that different papers have different textures. For example, tracing paper is smooth and thin, while watercolor paper is thick and textured. Materials can look and behave differently depending on the surface of the paper.

nodes.misconception: If the program runs, it must be correct.
nodes.response: Explain that a program can run but still be wrong if it doesn’t match the intended outcome. Debugging ensures accuracy.

nodes.misconception: Including personal materials in artwork has no effect on how emotional or powerful the art feels.
nodes.response: Remind children that artists might use personal materials to tell a story, share a memory, or express emotions.

nodes.misconception: Students spread images individually out across the page without making visual connections.
nodes.response: Encourage students to use overlapping and layering with their images to create interest and visual connections.

nodes.misconception: Defenders believe they can, or they try to, take the ball when they tag an opponent.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that the primary objective is to remove a tag from the ball carrier to stop their progress, rather than trying to take the ball.

nodes.misconception: When bowling, pupils focus solely on bowling powerfully and quickly every bowl, often causing them to bowl  inaccurately or without proper technique.
nodes.response: Ensure pupils understand that the accuracy of their bowling is crucial and that varying the speed and power of the bowls can actually make it trickier for the batter to hit the ball.

nodes.misconception: Target games must be played against people of similar ability or previous experience for it to be a fair competition.
nodes.response: Conditions can be put on specific players in target games to balance the competition, regardles of their ability or previous experience.

nodes.misconception: Pupils believe that all implemented tactics will always be successful.
nodes.response: Ensure pupils understand that tactics don't always work and they may need to react quickly to adapt them.

nodes.misconception: Typographic designs should be minimal because otherwise they are hard to read and do not communicate a clear message.
nodes.response: Typography enhances the clarity of a design, making text easier to read by arranging elements with a visual hierarchy.

nodes.misconception: Physical sketching is the same as sketching in parametric CAD.
nodes.response: Sketches in parametric CAD need to be constrained in order to create accurate and error free models.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think everyone will feel the same way when they hear a piece of music and respond with the same actions and expressions.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that we might feel and respond the same way, but it is just as likely that we will feel differently as a number of factors will influence how we feel, including our mood and experiences that day.

nodes.misconception: Scissors should be held with the thumb  on the bottom, and the index finger on the top.
nodes.response: Remind children that scissors should be used with the thumb on top, nearest to the ceiling. Scissors should also be held in the same position, cutting away from the body with the paper being moved.

nodes.misconception: Pupils choose movements and balances that only one pupil can perform as they are the actions they want to perform.
nodes.response: Support pupils to understand that they need to select movements and balances that both pupils in the pair can perform.

nodes.misconception: Pupils use the floor to create their linking movements in unison and move around the apparatus instead of using it.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that the apparatus is there to be used and that we can really enhance our creativity if we try and include a range of apparatus in our movements.

nodes.misconception: Pupils create bar models where the parts do not equal the whole or vice versa.
nodes.response: Whilst this may be a calculation error, it is important that the context of the story is considered when looking to re-adjust the bar model. Take time to work through the context again building the bar model from the what is known.

nodes.misconception: Pupils believe that when they use an attacking tactic it will always be successful.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that not all tactics work but they should continue to try hard and use a variety of tactics.

nodes.misconception: There are no 'rules' for writing a chord sequence.
nodes.response: While to some extent this is true, in Western classical music there are very typical patterns that are used very regularly. These include the position of perfect and imperfect cadences, and what the chords do throughout the 16 bars.

nodes.misconception: You can ask any question to add an item to a branching database.
nodes.response: You need to ask yes or no questions to add items to a branching database. Open-ended questions are too difficult to represent in a branching database.

nodes.misconception: That a theatre performance is all about actors interacting with each other on the stage.
nodes.response: Often the most memorable moments from a performance are the actors' monologues where they express their character's inner thoughts.

nodes.misconception: You cannot remove any work from your book or portfolio.
nodes.response: You should select your work carefully and on rare occasions you might find work that doesn't add to the creative journey and is best left out. Discuss these pieces with your teacher to get guidance first.

nodes.misconception: If you are writing about a character, you should just write down everything you know about them.
nodes.response: When writing about a character, you should consider how you interpret them and why. You should explain this main idea in your thesis.

nodes.misconception: Every quotation you write about should be analysed in detail.
nodes.response: Main quotations should be analysed, but you should also include supporting quotations that are embedded into sentences without analysis.

nodes.misconception: If we make a mistake in a performance we should start again.
nodes.response: When performing in front of an audience it's best to carry on if we make a mistake.  Most of the time the audience won't notice.

nodes.misconception: Hyperlinks only work on the homepage.
nodes.response: Hyperlinks are used across all pages, creating a fully navigable website. Any object on any HTML page can be made into a hyperlink.

nodes.misconception: Pupils get too nervous to perfom and find public speaking really daunting so they can't do it.
nodes.response: Even the most confident speakers feel nervous! It is completely natural to feel nervous when public speaking. Practising and using specfic strategies will mean they will gradually begin to understand how to work with them.

nodes.misconception: A mask shape must be perfectly symmetrical to look good.
nodes.response: While symmetry is often used, asymmetry can also be used to create dynamic and interesting designs.

nodes.misconception: Once the project has been programmed, it's finished.
nodes.response: It's important to test and debug to make sure the project works as intended. Look back at what was set as to what would make the project a success and consider how well the pogram carries out the task.

nodes.misconception: The pentatonic scale is limited to one octave on the instrument.
nodes.response: The pentatonic scale is just the names of the notes that we can use. You can use them as high-pitched notes or low-pitched notes on your instrument. Experiment with playing the scale up high and down low.

nodes.misconception: Websites require specialist knowledge to create and publish.
nodes.response: Drag-and-drop software and online platforms allow anyone to create and publish a website easily.

nodes.misconception: Using disjunct intervals in a melody means the notes can be placed anywhere.
nodes.response: Disjunct intervals need a sense of order to the music and should be used in some sort of pattern in the same way that conjunct intervals should.

nodes.misconception: That 'word blending' is a type of compound.
nodes.response: 'Word blending' combines only part of other words whereas word compounds combines the entirety of two existing words to form a new one.

nodes.misconception: All records must be filled in with text.
nodes.response: You can use tick boxes, numbers, or other formats to show data.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that patterns do not need a grid to be structured.
nodes.response: While freehand patterns exist, grids help maintain consistency.

nodes.misconception: Diction (articulation) is just about clear pronunciation.
nodes.response: Articulation is also connected to taking suitable singing breaths. If breathing is poorly controlled, consonants can sound weak or unclear, and vowels lose focus. Good breath support allows the voice to stay energised through quick or complex lyrics.

nodes.misconception: If there is a mistake in an audio recording, it will need to be re-recorded.
nodes.response: Small mistakes in audio can be trimmed without needing to re-record an entire vocal track. Small adjustments to audio are difficult to detect and can improve the quality of a track.

nodes.misconception: Repeating a shape many times will always create a pattern.
nodes.response: The turn angle must be correct to form a repeating design. With the wrong choice of value a pattern might not appear.

nodes.misconception: An algorithm cannot be represented in code.
nodes.response: An algorithm is a description of the instructions to follow so that a specified task can be completed. Therefore, algorithms can be converted and represented in to program code to enable a computer to carry out the solution to a task.

nodes.misconception: A sense of style in music refers only to the genre.
nodes.response: Style can mean genre-specific features but also can refer to compositional style and the composer using common features throughout a particular piece.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often fail to realise that they don't have to write from their own perspective.
nodes.response: Inform pupils that it can be incredibly powerful to write from another, imagined perspective.

nodes.misconception: The format and layout of slide decks must always be created from scratch each time you start a new document.
nodes.response: Slide deck templates have pre-designed layouts and formatting that can be used as a starting point when creating new slide decks.

nodes.misconception: All content found on the World Wide Web is free to reuse.
nodes.response: Content on the World Wide Web is subject to copyright and can be reused subject to licence agreements. Content found on the World Wide Web should be carefully chosen to ensure it is trustworthy and accurate.

nodes.misconception: The traditional story arc can only be applied to full narratives.
nodes.response: You can find elements of the traditional story arc in writing of any length.

nodes.misconception: Only paper and canvas are proper or professional surfaces for making art
nodes.response: Artists have long worked on a wide range of surfaces, including wood, metal, glass, fabric, cardboard, plastic, ceramics, and more. The surface is a creative choice, not a limitation.

nodes.misconception: If a rhythm includes quavers it is syncopated.
nodes.response: This is a common misconception when first learning syncopation. Reiterate that a rhythm is only syncopated if the emphasis is in between the main beats. In practice here, that means that there will be a quaver rest at the start of a beat.

nodes.misconception: A tone row is just a scale.
nodes.response: A tone row is different because it isn't just a set of notes to choose from, but a specific order. When you are composing something in C major, you can use the notes of the C major scale in any order. With a tone row, they have a specific order.

nodes.misconception: Proofreading your work is not important if you plan it.
nodes.response: Proofreading is equally important as planning. In pressured writing environments, we can easily make mistakes that we are not aware of.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may use 'ck' to representing the 'c' phoneme at the end of the word after a short vowel, like 'stick' and 'trick'.
nodes.response: Explain that in most words where the 'c' is at the end, it is represented as 'ck'. As this is a suffix, it doesn't follow usual rules. If we can spot a root word, and know that the new word is an adjective it will most likely be spelt 'ic'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think the suffix is spelt with a double 'l' like the word 'full'.
nodes.response: Explicitly point out the difference between the spelling of 'full' and the suffix 'ful'.

nodes.misconception: All joining methods are equally strong.
nodes.response: Some methods, like a tight twist are much stronger than others.

nodes.misconception: That descriptive writing is all about telling the reader what's in the image.
nodes.response: Descriptive writing is about showing the reader what's in the image through sensory and figurative language.

nodes.misconception: The microcontroller controls all systems at the same time.
nodes.response: In reality, most microcontrollers execute code sequentially, one line at a time. It may appear that microcontrollers are doing many things at once, but they’re actually switching between tasks quickly or handling them step by step.

nodes.misconception: The backbeat and off-beat are the same.
nodes.response: The backbeat is on beat 2 and 4 while the off-beat is on the second half of a beat (in between the beats).

nodes.misconception: Any notes will work for improvising
nodes.response: Find the balance between developing confidence in improvising and quality of musical ideas. Encourage pupils to think about the choice of notes, repetition, returning to a main note etc, as well as trying ideas and reflecting on what they sound like.

nodes.misconception: An ostinato, like the rhythm of a song, changes throughout a piece of music.
nodes.response: An ostinato does have a rhythm, but this rhythm is repeated over and over again throughout a piece of music. The rhythm stays exactly the same.

nodes.misconception: Python has a built-in XOR operator in the same way that it has AND, OR and NOT.
nodes.response: Unlike AND, OR and NOT, Python does not have a built-in operator for XOR and instead must be designed as part of and program that uses it.

nodes.misconception: Using the same rhythm in different ostinati creates effective contrast.
nodes.response: Using different rhythms in your ostinati is important for creating contrast. If they use the same rhythm, they will inevitably sound very similar. Try coming up with some interesting rhythm by clapping, then play them using notes on the keyboard.

nodes.misconception: Minimalism has no structure.
nodes.response: Minimalist music does have structure, but this might be on a micro level. It employs repetition of cells - a cyclical structure.

nodes.misconception: Improvised music has no structure.
nodes.response: Jazz pieces are heavily structured around chord sequences, the head and order of improvisatons.

nodes.misconception: In a debate you can only argue a stance you truly believe in.
nodes.response: Part of the skill of debating is being able to create, justify and convincingly present an argument that might not reflect your own personal viewpoint.

nodes.misconception: Creating and managing wilderness areas in the taiga biome is easy because the region is sparsely populated.
nodes.response: Managing wilderness areas in the taiga is challenging due to its extreme climate, vast size, remote location, and limited infrastructure, which make access, monitoring, and conservation efforts difficult.

nodes.misconception: Abstract collages need to have perfect symmetry or recognisable shapes.
nodes.response: Abstract collages don’t need symmetry or recognisable images. The beauty of abstraction lies in experimenting to create something visually engaging which can express ideas or emotions and finding balance through the arrangement.

nodes.misconception: When preparing for a performance, we should just focus on playing our own part accurately.
nodes.response: When playing and singing in an ensemble, the overall sound is important, we need to make the ensemble as cohesive and synchronised as possible.

nodes.misconception: Structures are all the same.
nodes.response: There are different types of structures - frame, shell and brick bonding structures. They are all used for different effects, purposes and reasons.

nodes.misconception: When you're making an animation, you need to make big changes to the drawing in each picture to make it move a lot.
nodes.response: To get smooth movement, you need to only make small changes to your drawing in each frame.

nodes.misconception: When gluing, always put the glue on the object that is being glued down.
nodes.response: By adding the glue to the backing instead of the object being glued down, it will prevent mess and reduce excess glue from being used. Additionally, use the a small amount of glue first as you can always add more glue.

nodes.misconception: You should select one quotation from each text in a comparative paragraph.
nodes.response: Like in a powerful analytical paragraph, selecting multiple quotations from each text will help strengthen your argument. Selecting these quotations in the planning stage is key.

nodes.misconception: One feature on its own will make a leitmotif have a particular mood.
nodes.response: The mood of a leitmotif comes from a combination of different musical elements, including melodic features. Changing one feature might slightly change the mood, but to create a strong mood you need to consider all different aspects of the leitmotif.

nodes.misconception: You have to include each aspect of characterisation in the same paragraph, and always in the same order.
nodes.response: Chaucer has a particular way of introducing and describing his characters. However, this is one way to do it, amongst many. You will see lots of different writers use the same methods of characterisation, but in different orders and structures.

nodes.misconception: Bitmap and raster are two different types of image.
nodes.response: They are the same and can be referred to as a raster or bitmap image.

nodes.misconception: Save and save as do the same thing.
nodes.response: Pressing save will save the file as the current filename and possibly overwrite an existing file. Selecting save as lets you specify a new file name and/or location.

nodes.misconception: You should only use certain colours that other artists use when creating artwork.
nodes.response: Art should be created to reflect your own style. Use colours that you think will make your artwork look the best.

nodes.misconception: It does not matter how the camera is positioned as long as the action is captured.
nodes.response: The camera angle can help portray a key element of the moment to the viewer and help them understand the meaning of the clip.

nodes.misconception: Using sophisticated vocabulary alone is enough to make my writing great.
nodes.response: Although sophisticated vocabulary is good, there are lots of smaller strategies that can also make writing effective.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often think the arrow in a food chain means “eats” or "depends on" and also that arrows should be drawn from predator to prey (rather than prey to predator).
nodes.response: This lesson reinforces the fact the the arrow in a food chain can be interpreted to mean 'is food for'.

nodes.misconception: The order of the blocks inside a 'forever' loop doesn't really matter, as long as they are all in there.
nodes.response: The order of the blocks inside a loop can matter, and running them in a different sequence may affect the game.

nodes.misconception: Vector drawings cannot be edited.
nodes.response: Each element added to a vector drawing is an editable object.

nodes.misconception: We need to describe sounds in a scene merely to tick off the fact we have used sensory language.
nodes.response: Thinking of scenarios where sound is particularly important can help us to use sound imagery more effectively.

nodes.misconception: Evidence, or quotations, need to be long when used in an analytical paragraph or response.
nodes.response: If you select the right words, single words can provide an opportunity for rich analysis. Layering your comments means you can say a lot about a little!

nodes.misconception: A list index starts at 1 as that is the first element in the list and should be counted as the first item.
nodes.response: In most programming languages, list indexing is zero-based, which means the index starts at 0. The number indicates the position before the value is seen.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often find it difficult to know what order logic gates should be evaluated. Without brackets, there is still an order of precedence.
nodes.response: Remind pupils of how the order of precedence in maths is applied to calculations. In a similarway, logic gates should be evaluated in the order: brackets, NOT, AND, OR.

nodes.misconception: Monoprinting is only about making a copy, not about creativity.
nodes.response: Remind children that monoprinting is a form of artistic expression. Artists can use monoprinting to create unique, creative works where textures, colours and styles can vary greatly.

nodes.misconception: As long as I keep my headline and subheading short, they will be effective.
nodes.response: Headlines and subheadings must be crafted to fit the purpose of the article.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that all nouns are a person, place or thing that you can touch.
nodes.response: Show a range of different nouns, including common and abstract nouns.  Show that they can be described with an adjective.

nodes.misconception: It is quicker to create a pictogram by hand than trying to create one on a computer.
nodes.response: When creating a pictogram on a computer, it is much quicker and the pictures will be uniform in appearance. Working on a computer also has the benefit of being able to make changes quickly and easily without having to redo the entire pictogram.

nodes.misconception: Accompaniments only use on-beat rhythm patterns to help keep us in time.
nodes.response: Accompaniments can use any rhythms! Syncopated rhythms and polyrhythms can still keep us in time as we feel the offbeat and still feel the steady pulse.

nodes.misconception: Computers always have screens so that the user knows what processing has been performed.
nodes.response: Computers can carry actions using a variety of output devices. Physical computers are often used to carry out physical actions based on detected inputs so do not need a screen to display information.

nodes.misconception: Any pitch and notes can work in a composition.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to think about the choice of notes in their musical ideas and listen to how it sounds.

nodes.misconception: When pupils add more content to their sequence, they can lose flow with the sequence looking unpolished. Pupils show limited variety in their locomotive elements.
nodes.response: Practise the sequence slowly at first, focusing on smooth transitions between movements and balances. Encourage pupils to be creative and add variety to their locomotive movements throughout the sequence.

nodes.misconception: Pupils will often move too close to the ball and not give themselves enough room to hit the ball accurately. Pupils will often hit the ball with too much power and a lack of control.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that the ball should be in front and slightly to the side of their body when they make contact with the ball. Pupils should be given time to  experiment with the amount of power needed to hit the targets, and encourage a smooth swing.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may change to an overarm throw when you are asking them to aim for the back of the court. Pupils may take too many risks when aiming for the perimeter and the ball goes out/hits the net a lot.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to step into their throw and follow throught towards their target to get more power behind their throw. Although we want pupils to aim away from the midle of the court, we still want them to successfully throw into the court area.

nodes.misconception: Crowding around the ball
nodes.response: By taking the ball out into the wide channels on a pitch/court, you draw defenders out of their area and create space elsewhere to pass to your own players and make an attack on goal.

nodes.misconception: Templates do not need to be pinned to fabric.
nodes.response: Remind children that pinning before cutting allows you to adjust the placement of your templates.

nodes.misconception: Pupils try to record their new ideas into one of the pitched instrument tracks.
nodes.response: Demonstrate this error before they have time to improvise new ideas.

nodes.misconception: You can never use slang, colloquialisms and idioms in narrative writing.
nodes.response: If slang, colloquialism and idioms are part of your narrative voice, it is okay to use them but you have to ensure your use of them comes across as deliberate, consistent and that you have secure grammar and control over the piece of work.

nodes.misconception: Commas and full stops are interchangeable.
nodes.response: Full stops divide independent clauses and create a longer pause than a comma. Full stops divide ideas and create clear writing. Commas divide subordinate clauses and lists. They create a shorter pause.

nodes.misconception: Christians and Jews all understand the creation story in the same way.
nodes.response: There are different ways to interpret and understand the creation stories in the Bible.

nodes.misconception: There is only one creation story.
nodes.response: Genesis 1 and 2 both tell the story of creation. Genesis 1 focuses on the creation of the universe, and Genesis 2 focuses on the creation of humanity. Genesis 3 is also linked to creation and focuses on the Fall of humanity.

nodes.misconception: When performing sequences, some pupils perform too many actions, the sequence goes on for far too long and quality can be lost.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that sequences should have a beginning, a middle and an end so they can remember and repeat it. It is better to have a short, high quality sequence than a long, low quality one.

nodes.misconception: Practise makes perfect. Pupils forget the variety of shapes they can use for gymnastics skills and default to using the same basic balances and jumps in every sequence.
nodes.response: Practise might not always make a performance perfect, but it will make actions and sequences improve. Pupils can work together to help use practise time to improve. Display posters or lists of shape ideas for jumps, rolls and balances.

nodes.misconception: A content creator must always promote an event through posters and videos to be successful.
nodes.response: Remind children that while posters and videos are useful, an event can also be successfully promoted through spoken messages, social media, or written adverts. The key is to share clear and engaging information, not just the format used.

nodes.misconception: A fashion collection is an assortment of clothes and accessories with no common theme or coordinating colours.
nodes.response: Remind children that a fashion collection consists of clothes and accessories that share colours, fabrics, or themes designed to showcase the particular style of a fashion designer.

nodes.misconception: A game's aesthetic does not need to be consistent throughout the game.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that keeping the graphics, sounds, colours and feelings the same throughout the game helps players stay focused and understand the game better.

nodes.misconception: It is not important to consider the identity of the festival when creating your logo.
nodes.response: Remind children that graphic designers should consider the unique character of their festival when creating their logo, so they can visually represent the ethos of the event in their design.

nodes.misconception: Makeup is only used to cover imperfections and cannot be used to tell a story, represent a theme or have fun with one's appearance.
nodes.response: Remind children that makeup is much more than decoration. It is a powerful way to express identity, emotions and celebration, and it helps bring people together in shared joy and creativity.

nodes.misconception: Harmony and chords are the same thing.
nodes.response: Although the harmony is created by the different notes of the chord progression, harmony also includes all parts in the music including the melodic line.

nodes.misconception: A rhetorical question is never answered. It is designed to make people think.
nodes.response: While a rhetorical question is designed to encourage the reader or audience to consider their views on the subject matter, a writer can choose to answer the rhetorical question conveying their opinions (but they don't have to).

nodes.misconception: Fear of falling or not clearing the obstacle can lead to hesitation which can then affect the flow and overall success of the vault.
nodes.response: Gradual progression and practising on lower obstacles can help build confidence.

nodes.misconception: The Romantics were known for writing about love and romance.
nodes.response: The Romantics are not to be confused with 'romantics' who may write love poetry. The Romantics most commonly wrote about nature and were known for critiquing the direction of society's progress.

nodes.misconception: Critical thinking focuses on judging artworks as 'good' or 'bad'.
nodes.response: Critical thinking  helps artists and audiences to think deeply about art and respect different viewpoints.

nodes.misconception: Design critique and design evaluation are the same.
nodes.response: Design critique evaluates a product to improve it, a design evaluation evaluates an end product against criteria.

nodes.misconception: A cross-sectional drawing is just another drawing view, such as front or side.
nodes.response: A cross-sectional view is an internal view showing what the inside looks like when sliced through. It is is meant to reveal hidden details inside an object.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may have difficultly partitioning 10s when crossing the 100s boundary. (e.g. 125 - 40)
nodes.response: Pupils practice adding to/subtracting from multiples of 10 (e.g. 130 - 50) before exploring non-multiples of 10 (e.g. 85 + 30)

nodes.misconception: Confusion regarding the number before the decade numbers, e.g. saying 30, 39
nodes.response: Explicitly look at the patterns in numbers that precede a decade number and discuss errors.

nodes.misconception: Confusion around the numbers which cross the tens boundary, e.g. 39, 40 may say 39, 30
nodes.response: Make errors for the children to discuss; encourage them to  explain and correct mistakes.

nodes.misconception: Confusion between the number after 29, 39 etc. so saying 29,20 or twenty-none, twenty -ten.
nodes.response: Explicitly look at the numbers that follow a number ending in 9 using stem sentence to support.

nodes.misconception: Pupils sometimes use the terms evaporation and boiling interchangeably, but they are not the same.
nodes.response: Boiling: a liquid substance is heated and gas bubbles form. Evaporation: same, BUT only on the surface of the liquid, no bubbles form and the gas mixes with air.

nodes.misconception: Divisions can only be arranged as regular rows and columns.
nodes.response: By using divisions within other divisions any layout of a page is possible.

nodes.misconception: It is easier to apply CSS directly to the HTML tags as they are used.
nodes.response: There is little time saved by applying CSS directly to tags and it generates more work later if the same changes need to be made in different parts of a web page.

nodes.misconception: Knowing and using one listening strategy is enough.
nodes.response: All three sets of strategies work together, and you should be flexible in applying them as needed throughout the listening process.

nodes.misconception: The first thing I hear correctly and understand is usually the answer to a listening comprehension question.
nodes.response: It is important to listen to the whole text before answering a listening comprehension question, as information may not be presented in an obvious order.

nodes.misconception: The only translation of 've' in Spanish is 'she, he, it sees'.
nodes.response: In Spanish, the verb 've' usually means 'she, he, it sees', but it is also the affirmative imperative form of 'ir', meaning 'go'.

nodes.misconception: To tell somebody who is familiar to you to do something, use the 2nd person singular form of the verb.
nodes.response: To tell somebody who is familiar to you to do something, use the affirmative imperative. For -ar verbs this ends in -a, and for -er/-ir verbs this ends in -e.

nodes.misconception: When artists make work about identity, they reveal all aspects of themselves.
nodes.response: Artists make selections about what to conceal or reveal in their work.

nodes.misconception: A good portfolio presentation should be is highly decorative and colourful to be engaging.
nodes.response: While creative touches like washi tape or coloured paint can add personality, a clean and minimal layout can be just as effective, sometimes even more so. The goal is to curate a cohesive presentation that supports your work, not distracts from it

nodes.misconception: In gymnastics, we only do forward and backward rolls. We bring our feet up to our bottom in a tuck jump.
nodes.response: Rolls can be sideways; as long as pupils roll silently with control, they are still successful. We bring our feet and knees up towards our chest in a tuck jump.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often refer to the turns of a coil as the number of coils.
nodes.response: Emphasise that turns of wire can be added to a coil to make the coil longer.

nodes.misconception: Balances are not held still for long enough.
nodes.response: Practise balancing still and remind pupils that they should be held still for about 4 seconds. Pupils can try focusing on a fixed spot to help them keep still. If they close their eyes to balance, they will wobble - try this too!

nodes.misconception: Pupils lean backwards in a teddy bear roll, ending up on their back and getting stuck there.
nodes.response: Stress the importance of leaning to the side (left or right) on a shoulder and placing it close to their knee to start the action, then lifting the opposite leg (not both) to help you face the opposite direction.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think they can create a pathway by drawing the letter shapes in the air.
nodes.response: Drawing letter shapes in the air produces 'air pathways'. This lesson is focusing on 'floor pathways' which require the pupils to travel along the shapes of the different letters.

nodes.misconception: The cuisine, ingredients and food customs in different countries have not changed over time.
nodes.response: History has changed the cuisine, ingredients and food customs. This has happened because of travel, trade and wars.

nodes.misconception: All protests are loud and dangerous.
nodes.response: Protest can be peaceful and placards can be a safe way to share ideas.

nodes.misconception: Artists only make artwork with images.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that artists can make artwork with images, but they can also create artwork with words.

nodes.misconception: William I introduced a whole new social system called the feudal system which was completely different from what came before.
nodes.response: In fact, many of the features of what became known as the feudal system were already in place in Anglo-Saxon England. William took the opportunity to increase his control over society to enable the extraction of wealth; his successors built on this.

nodes.misconception: Learners may think that the life of every child in Tanzania (and Africa) is like the life of Zahra.
nodes.response: Spend more time discussing the similarities and differences between people in the UK to help learners appreciate that there will be many similarities and differences in people's lives both within and between countries and places.

nodes.misconception: Understanding the ethics of research practices is complex and often misunderstood. The details of various brain scanning techniques are complex and also confusing.
nodes.response: Ethical practices are discussed with examples and changes through history to give context. Brain scanning techniques are illustrated and explained, with follow up tasks.

nodes.misconception: Understanding the ethics of research practices is complex and often misunderstood. The details of various brain scanning techniques are complex and also confusing.
nodes.response: Ethical practices are discussed with examples and changes through history to give context. Brain scanning techniques are illustrated and explained, with follow up tasks.

nodes.misconception: Mains appliances draw all their electricity from the live wire, without need for a complete circuit.
nodes.response: Show pupils live and neutral wires connected to a AC connections on a power pack (you can use individual wires taken from mains cables) to show complete circuits are necessary, and that mains cables contain these wires.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that different parts of a food chain are independent of each other and are not impacted by changes elsewhere in the food chain.
nodes.response: Clear explanation of how each part of a food chain is linked to other parts of the chain and how even small changes can have a big impact throughout a food chain.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that bees are the only animals that pollinate plants or that bees are the only pollinators currently in decline.
nodes.response: Explain that many types of insects, as well as some birds and mammals, can be pollinators and that many of these animal species are also in decline.

nodes.misconception: The safelight allows any kind of light to be on in the darkroom without damaging prints.
nodes.response: The safelight is not a “free pass” for unlimited light exposure and that all light exposure must be controlled and time-sensitive.

nodes.misconception: You need a strong throw to be good at darts.
nodes.response: Darts is more about control and accuracy than power. A smooth, balanced stance and consistent release are more important.

nodes.misconception: Many students believe that Darwin was the only scientist involved in the development of the theory of evolution by natural selection.
nodes.response: This lesson directly addresses this misconception and includes examples of other scientists who were involved in the original and later development of the theory.

nodes.misconception: Adjectives in German don't have endings.
nodes.response: Adjectives have endings when they precede a noun. Compare 'der Hund ist groß' with 'der große Hund ist schwarz'. Adjective endings agree in case, gender and number with nouns. There are useful tables that can be learned to support correct usage.

nodes.misconception: The German subject pronoun 'man' must always be translated using the English subject pronoun 'one'.
nodes.response: 'Man' has a range of possible translations, including 'people' and 'you'. It can also be used to say what 'is done' or 'was done' by people in general.

nodes.misconception: For verb stems ending in ‘-el’, remove the 'e' from the stem in all present tense forms.
nodes.response: For verb stems ending in ‘-el’, remove the 'e' from the stem in the first person singular of the present tense only.

nodes.misconception: There is only one way to form the plural in German.
nodes.response: German has several rules for forming plurals. The best way to correctly form plurals is to learn the rules and frequently practise them.

nodes.misconception: All sentences with 'wenn' use word order 3 and send the verb to the end.
nodes.response: Distinguish between a clause and a sentence. 'Wenn' clauses need a second clause to complete a sentence. A clause starting with 'wenn' sends the verb to the end. If the 'wenn' clause is first, the second clause (after the comma) uses inversion.

nodes.misconception: The imperfect tense is only ever written.
nodes.response: Whilst the imperfect tense is mainly used to narrate past events in written German, some forms are regularly used in spoken German, such as 'es gab', 'war' and 'hatte'.

nodes.misconception: Verbs have the same meaning whether they are used reflexively or non-reflexively.
nodes.response: Some verbs have the same or similar meanings when used reflexively and non-reflexively, e.g. nennen, to call; sich nennen, to call oneself. However, some verbs completely change their meaning, e.g. anziehen, to attract; sich anziehen, to get dressed.

nodes.misconception: To analyse data you just need to explain what the data is demonstrating.
nodes.response: The analysis skill goes a little further and looks at patterns / trends / relationships in the context of data provided.

nodes.misconception: Only one value can be shown on a graph.
nodes.response: Different values can be broken down into different categories, such as the age of people and their participation in different activities, which gives a more detailed picture of participants.

nodes.misconception: It is only possible to present quantitative data.
nodes.response: Qualitative data can be presented in other formats to summarise findings.

nodes.misconception: Once data is stored in a database, it’s automatically safe and private.
nodes.response: Just storing data in a database does not make it secure. Data must be protected with proper privacy measures.

nodes.misconception: If you have missing data and cannot find the original source, there is nothing you can do.
nodes.response: You could look at similar data and generate an average value to insert. For example, if the zoo is missing a weight for a lion, they could calculate the average weight of the other lions and enter this.

nodes.misconception: Graphs in exam questions will have the x and y axes labelled.
nodes.response: One of the skills assessed in GCSE PE exam questions is to label the x and y axes, as well as plot data and present as the method requested by the question.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to write response boxes that do not overlap for continuous data.
nodes.response: Remind pupils of how to write intervals using inequality symbols.

nodes.misconception: A model can be improved by providing more training data.
nodes.response: Although a large data set is important, more data doesn't necessarily improve output. It is important that training data is high-quality, accurate and diverse.

nodes.misconception: If you gather data for a minute or two to check that the data collected looks ok, your experiment will be successful.
nodes.response: There might be other factors that affect your experiment, which are out of your control. For example, someone could unplug your data logger, the batteries might run out or the data may be corrupt due to an issue with the hardware or software.

nodes.misconception: Cases are just boxes for a data logger to fit into.
nodes.response: Cases need to display the micro:bit, some of the components and fit the battery packs

nodes.misconception: Traffic surveys are only about collecting data.
nodes.response: Data collected from the data loggers can be used to understand what is happening in an environment and make suggestions for improvements.

nodes.misconception: A variable is a set piece of data that can not change once collected.
nodes.response: A variable is a named piece of data stored in a computer’s memory, accessed and changed by a computer program.

nodes.misconception: SQL statements can only be used with exisiting tables.
nodes.response: SQL statements can be used to perform other actions on a databse such as creating new tables.

nodes.misconception: Data is sent all at once as one big file.
nodes.response: Data is split into packets, sent separately and then reassembled.

nodes.misconception: Proprietary software always costs money.
nodes.response: Proprietary software is usually sold to end users, although sometimes it is available for free.

nodes.misconception: Data science is just about collecting loads of data.
nodes.response: Data science isn’t just about gathering data, it’s about understanding data and using it to make decisions or discoveries.

nodes.misconception: Python will automatically round numbers to the nearest whole number.
nodes.response: Python will perform calculations based on the values that have been provided and generate an answer that can include fractional parts. If you want to reduce the number of digits, you can use the round() function.

nodes.misconception: Arrays are always the best choice for storing and accessing collections of data.
nodes.response: While arrays offer efficient direct access to elements using their index, they have limitations, such as fixed size and potential inefficiency in terms of unused elements.

nodes.misconception: Data validation can only check values entered into a cell. It cannot be used to stop a user from leaving a cell blank.
nodes.response: Data validation can be used to prevent users from leaving required cells blank.

nodes.misconception: A DBMS is only used for storing data.
nodes.response: While storage is a major function, a DBMS also provides data security, integrity and querying capabilities.

nodes.misconception: A primary key and a foreign key are the same thing.
nodes.response: A primary key is an attribute that uniquely identifies a record in a database table, whereas a foreign key is an attribute in one table that is the primary key in another table and is used to link the tables together.

nodes.misconception: The database tells you the 'best' option automatically.
nodes.response: The database provides data, but users must decide which option is best by comparing data in fields like price, duration and times. The 'best' choice depends on the situation.

nodes.misconception: Like in English, the SSCs [an] and [em] sound different: January and December.
nodes.response: The SSCs [an], [en], [am], and [em] sound the same in French: 'janvier' and 'décembre'

nodes.misconception: '¿Qué?' and '¿cuál?' are always interchangeable when asking for dates: '¿Qué es la fecha?' and '¿Cuál es la fecha?' are both correct.
nodes.response: The natural way to ask the date in Spanish is '¿Cuál es la fecha de hoy?'. 'Cuál' is followed by ‘es’ and 'qué' is followed by a noun.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may not realise that David is seen as a prophet in the Islamic tradition.
nodes.response: David is seen as a prophet. However, as he repented, he did not sin.

nodes.misconception: Children may not know that light travels in straight lines, this mans they would not understand why half of the Earth is always in darkness.
nodes.response: Use a globe and torch in a dark room to demonstrate that only the side of the globe facing the torch will receive light. The other half remains in darkness.

nodes.misconception: We have the same amount of daylight in every season.
nodes.response: Explanation of how day length changes throughout the year and is longer during summer. You may link back to a previous lesson: Day length in winter (in the Year 1 unit: Seasonal changes: autumn and winter).

nodes.misconception: We have the same amount of daylight in every season.
nodes.response: Explanation of how day length changes throughout the year and is shorter during winter.

nodes.misconception: Adjectives do not have plurals forms, like English.
nodes.response: In Spanish, adjectives match the nouns they describe. If the noun is singular, the adjective will be singular as well, and the same for plural nouns.

nodes.misconception: Spanish days of the week start with a capital letter as in English.
nodes.response: Spanish does not capitalise the days of the week.

nodes.misconception: NGBs only support elite sport at the top of their game.
nodes.response: NGBs provide support from grass roots level all the way up to elite level sport.

nodes.misconception: The stress in 'me gustaría' falls on the second syllable 'ta'.
nodes.response: The stress in 'me gustaría' falls on the 'í'. We can tell this because it has an accent.

nodes.misconception: The stress in 'me gustaría' falls on the second syllable 'ta'.
nodes.response: The stress in 'me gustaría' falls on the 'í'. We can tell this because it has an accent.

nodes.misconception: It is sufficient to give one-word answers in a role-play.
nodes.response: In a role-play pupils need to answer each question with a short phrase or sentence.

nodes.misconception: The verb 'hacer' follows the same rule as 'poner' for forming the 1st person singular of the present tense.
nodes.response: The letter 'g' replaces the 'c' in hacer in the first person singular of the present tense.

nodes.misconception: I should include as much detail as possible in role-play answers.
nodes.response: When performing a role-play, answers should contain one verb and be concise. Do not add unnecessary detail.

nodes.misconception: I should include as much detail as possible in role-play answers.
nodes.response: When perfoming a role-play, answers should contain one verb and be concise. Do not add unnecessary detail.

nodes.misconception: The only factor in understanding listening tasks is vocabulary. If I know enough words, I don’t need any strategies to comprehend what I hear.
nodes.response: A strong knowledge of high frequency vocabulary is key to unlocking effective listening comprehension. However, strategies such as prediction, synonym recognition and identifying distractors can also improve listening skills.

nodes.misconception: Modal verbs like 'quiero' can be followed with a 1st person singular verb like 'compro'.
nodes.response: Modal verbs like 'quiero' must be followed with an infinitive verb like 'comprar'. For example, 'I want to buy' in Spanish is 'quiero comprar'.

nodes.misconception: Modal verbs like 'quiero' can be followed with a 1st person singular verb like 'compro'.
nodes.response: Modal verbs like 'quiero' must be followed with an infinitive verb like 'comprar'. For example, 'I want to buy' in Spanish is 'quiero comprar'.

nodes.misconception: The only way to mean 'you (sg)' in Spanish is 'tú'.
nodes.response: There are two ways to mean 'you (sg)' in Spanish. Use 'tú' to mean 'you' in an informal context, and 'usted' to mean 'you' in a formal context.

nodes.misconception: The Spanish translation of 'the money is hers' (for exampl) is 'el dinero es suya' because the owner is feminine.
nodes.response: The Spanish translation of 'the money is hers' is 'el dinero es suyo' because the object is masculine. Possessive adjectives agree with the object, not the owner.

nodes.misconception: As in the present tense, -er and -ir verbs have different endings in the preterite tense.
nodes.response: Verbs ending in -er and -ir have the same endings in the preterite tense.

nodes.misconception: When answering questions, I can use the verb in the question to start my answer.
nodes.response: You can start your answer using the question verb but it's important to not copy the question word-for-word. If questions use 2nd person verbs, you need to change them to 1st person, changing 'you' verbs into 'I' or 'we' forms.

nodes.misconception: To say 'when I am older I will work in a hospital', say 'cuando soy mayor trabajaré en un hospital'.
nodes.response: To say 'when I am older I will work in a hospital', say 'cuando sea mayor trabajaré en un hospital'. After 'cuando', use the subjunctive to talk about an event that hasn't yet happened.

nodes.misconception: To say 'when I am older I will work in a hospital', say 'cuando soy mayor trabajaré en un hospital'.
nodes.response: To say 'when I am older I will work in a hospital', say 'cuando sea mayor trabajaré en un hospital'. After 'cuando', use the subjunctive to talk about an event that hasn't yet happened.

nodes.misconception: I should develop my answers as much as possible for all parts of the speaking exam.
nodes.response: It is not necessary to develop your answers extensively for all parts of the speaking exam. Remember to keep your answers short and succinct in the role-play section.

nodes.misconception: I should develop my answers as much as possible for all parts of the speaking exam.
nodes.response: It is not necessary to develop your answers extensively for all parts of the speaking exam. Remember to keep your answers short and succinct in the role-play section.

nodes.misconception: There is not much I can do to prepare for the listening exam.
nodes.response: You can prepare for the listening exam by revising vocabulary and being ready to listen out for synonyms and distractors.

nodes.misconception: There is not much I can do to prepare for the listening exam.
nodes.response: You can prepare for the listening exam by revising vocabulary and being ready to listen out for synoynms and distractors.

nodes.misconception: The Buddhist belief in rebirth teaches that after death, a persons 'soul' is reborn in to another living being.
nodes.response: The Buddha taught that nothing is permenent, everything changes (anicca) and there is no fixed self or soul (anatta). Rebirth may be described as a person's ‘energy’ being reborn, rather than a fixed soul.

nodes.misconception: That mummification is just a case of wrapping a body in bandages and burying it.
nodes.response: There are several stages in the mummification process, each of which must be done precisely and carefully in order to be successful.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may find the distinction between discussion and philosophical questions challenging.
nodes.response: Encourage them to imagine asking the question to their parent or headteacher - if the person could answer without having read 'Romeo and Juliet', then it's a philosophical question. Model this process.

nodes.misconception: There is one interpretation of a text and it is your job as a student of English to find the correct interpretation.
nodes.response: Texts rarely have one interpretation, and part of your job as a student of English is to consider the range and then select which one you think is the strongest, whilst still allowing for the idea that some might disagree with you.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that deforestation only has negative impacts.
nodes.response: Trees and the deforested land can provide many benefits for humans.

nodes.misconception: There is an endless supply of fossil fuels on Earth.  There are no downsides to electric cars.
nodes.response: Teaching slides will explain that fossil fuel is a finite resource. Children will have the chance to research the pros and cons of electric cars. Feedback slides will clarify these.

nodes.misconception: Only new programmers will have bugs in their programs.
nodes.response: Every programmer will need to correct errors and debug their code. Part of the process of programming is correcting mistakes made as you go along. Regluarly test your program does what it needs to as you go along.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that deception is only about tricking your opponent with flashy shots (e.g. through the legs).
nodes.response: Effective deception is about subtle changes in timing, swing and shot placement. It doesn’t always require exaggerated fakes - small delays or slight adjustments can be just as effective in disrupting your opponent’s rhythm.

nodes.misconception: When using adjustment (e.g. 456 − 199), pupils may forget whether they have to subtract or add 1 after they have subtracted 200
nodes.response: Ask pupils if they subtract 200 then subtract 1 more, how much have they subtracted altogether? They should see that they have subtracted 201, not 199 A number line representation will support pupil's understanding with this.

nodes.misconception: Children may have difficulty interpreting the problem and be unsure whether to ignore or include the remainder in the answer.
nodes.response: Throughout, ask and encourage children to articulate what each part of the equation represents from the problem in order to link the concrete and the abstract representation.

nodes.misconception: Some children can become concerned that there are rules about when to use a pen and when to use a pencil. This can slow them down and take the focus from the task.
nodes.response: Remind the children of the questions in this lesson. What are the attributes of the tools and which is best suited for the task? Remind them that there are no set rules and sometimes it can come down to personal preference.

nodes.misconception: Children may think that speeches do not need to have a specific purpose.
nodes.response: A speaker must consider their purpose for speaking before they write their speech so they know what impact they wish to have on the audience

nodes.misconception: All worldviews have completely different ideas about how to live a good life.
nodes.response: Worldviews share some ideas, such as the Golden Rule.

nodes.misconception: All trees have leaves that they lose every year.
nodes.response: Show a range of examples of different types of trees including evergreen.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think to solve a problem has a just one single option.
nodes.response: Problem solving is not linear, nor is there only one universal problem solving technique. The right approach depends on the nature of the problem in a specific context.

nodes.misconception: 'De' is always translated as 'to' in English.
nodes.response: 'De' is often translated as 'to'. However, it can be translated as 'from' and is sometimes not translated at all.

nodes.misconception: Exclamatory sentences are the only sentences that express emotions
nodes.response: Interrogative sentences can also effectively show some emotions e.g. confusion, despair, by the character asking themselves questions

nodes.misconception: Opinions are just what you think and don't need to be informed by anything.
nodes.response: Opinions should be informed by available information or evidence. For example: prior knowledge, contextual information and the writer's language choices, can all help to create informed opinions.

nodes.misconception: Rhythm grid notation only shows one instruction - play and rest.
nodes.response: Rhythm grid notation can give many instructions, including which instrument to play.

nodes.misconception: The effects of decolonisation were positive for countries newly independent from the British Empire.
nodes.response: For many newly independent nations, freedom brought many difficulties as well as benefits.

nodes.misconception: The borders drawn during Partition were clear and accepted by all.
nodes.response: The Radcliffe Line, which demarcated the borders, was highly contentious and led to significant disputes and confusion, which resulted in violence.

nodes.misconception: All Irish nationalists shared the same views and had the same aims.
nodes.response: Some Irish nationalists wanted Home Rule for Ireland whereas other nationalists (known as republicans) wanted complete independence from Britain. After 1921, republicans split between those who supported the Anglo-Irish Treaty and those who did not.

nodes.misconception: That Britain has no historic role in the creation of tension between Arabs and Jews over Palestine.
nodes.response: Britain's colonial role in Palestine during and after the First World War involved it making conflicting promises to both Arabs and Jews over Palestine's future.

nodes.misconception: All Caribbean countries gained independence from Britain at the same time.
nodes.response: Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago were the first of Britain's Caribbean colonies to achieve independence in 1962, however, the last British colony in the Caribbean to gain independence was Saint Kitts and Nevis in 1983.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that once the base is painted the 3D artwork is completed.
nodes.response: Artists often reflect and revisit their work to add further detail and bring their artwork to life.

nodes.misconception: 'Nous' always means 'we' in French.
nodes.response: 'Nous' means 'we' when used as a subject pronoun. 'Nous' means 'us' when used as an emphatic pronoun.

nodes.misconception: 'Nous' always means 'we' in French.
nodes.response: 'Nous' means 'we' when used as a subject pronoun. 'Nous' means 'us' when used as an emphatic pronoun.

nodes.misconception: Pupil can often get confused with increasing and decreasing an amount e.g Increase 45 by 23% and decreasing 45 by 23% have the same multiplier.
nodes.response: Encourage students to draw double number lines or ratio tables so they can see the increase and multiplier or decrease and multiplier.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that simply ensuring a fair test will improve data collecting in a practical.
nodes.response: Evaluating a practical is an often overlooked skill.  Challenge pupils to focus on the equipment chosen and/or the method followed to consider how better data might be collected.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that simply ensuring a fair test will improve data collecting in a practical.
nodes.response: Evaluating a practical is an often overlooked skill.  Challenge pupils to focus on the equipment chosen and/or the method followed to consider how better data might be collected.

nodes.misconception: Only finding the product of the integers and fractional parts when multiplying mixed numbers.
nodes.response: Link back to the area model, there will be 2 parts which they have not found the area of.

nodes.misconception: 40 thousands placing the 4 in the thousands column.
nodes.response: As there are 40 thousands the 4 is in the ten thousands column.

nodes.misconception: Only seeing the amount, not proportion.  E.g £30 from £100 is no different to £30 from £60.
nodes.response: Referring to the whole using bar models or fractions can emphasise the amount with respect to the whole.

nodes.misconception: Deepfakes are easy to spot because they always look fake or glitchy
nodes.response: Many deepfakes today are highly realistic and difficult to detect, especially when viewed quickly or shared on social media. As technology improves, deepfakes can mimic real people’s voices and faces with convincing detail.

nodes.misconception: Installing antivirus software is enough to fully protect my device from malware.
nodes.response: Antivirus software is helpful, but it’s only one part of a broader defence strategy. Full protection also requires regular software updates, strong passwords, safe browsing habits and user awareness to avoid phishing and suspicious downloads.

nodes.misconception: Pupils tend to chase after the ball and they all gravitate towards it as opposed to the player they are marking.
nodes.response: Focus on staying close to your opponent, wait for the pass to come to them and then attempt to intercept it.

nodes.misconception: Pupils mark the same pupil, leaving attackers open in space. Pupils swarm around and only mark the player with the ball.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to communicate and ensure everyone is responsible for a different player. Remind pupils of the rule concerning marking. This rule is in place to enable the pupil in possession to look up and make effective passing decisions.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often believe they can use physical contact to tackle or push their opponent.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that tag rugby is a non-contact sport and pupils can only tag their opponents or intercept a pass.

nodes.misconception: Failing to remain goal side whilst keeping a view on the player and the ball.
nodes.response: Failing to remain goal side of your opposition exposes yourself to an easy scoring opportunity.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that when you are player-to -player marking it is only about being an individual.
nodes.response: Defenders must communicate, adjust to overloads and support each other. If one defender gets beaten, others need to be ready to help. Marking your player is just one part of working together to stop the attack.

nodes.misconception: Pupils forget who to mark, leaving some attackers unmarked and free to pass and move.
nodes.response: Pupils need to work as a team to agree who they are marking so they can apply pressure effectively.

nodes.misconception: When defending in a game situation, pupils tend to follow the ball which closes up the space and leaves other players unmarked.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that they need to stay close to the player they are marking and be prepared to intercept the ball when it is passed to their opponent.

nodes.misconception: There is certainly a misconception with many pupils that the ball should be hit out into the field whenever possible, exacerbated by the need to do this in many other striking and fielding games.
nodes.response: Pupils should understand on occasions in cricket, blocking or leaving the ball are actually preferable shots to play, rather than shots with a higher risk of getting out. It requires a different mindset to a lot of other striking and fielding games.

nodes.misconception: Pupils are deflated and lack self-motivation if their team does not have possession of the ball.
nodes.response: Get pupils to think carefully about the tactics and strategies that can be used to prevent the attack from scoring and help the defensive team regain possession.

nodes.misconception: Once a player has released the ball, the defenders' work is done.
nodes.response: Stage 3 defending can be used to impact the next phase of play.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that Korfball is a contact sport where you can push players.
nodes.response: Korfball allows incidental contact that is natural movement, e.g. brushing shoulders and close marking, however pushing, holding or blocking is not allowed.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think a defensive player must catch the ball outright on initial contact from a shot.
nodes.response: It is sometimes more effective to bump a rebound up in the air for a teammate to catch, but it does then count as a pass. Whereas if you catch it cleanly or catch your own rebound, it doesn't use up one of your passes.

nodes.misconception: Pupils rush when discussing their tactics as they just want to play the game. Not all pupils get to contribute to the team discussions.
nodes.response: Praise and celebrate teams who discuss their tactics thoroughly, ensuring everyone contributes and that everyone understands.

nodes.misconception: Pupils tend to define a product that they wish to design and make at this point. They become fixated on a design.
nodes.response: Pupils need to keep their design brief open so that it does not create design fixation.
