nodes.response: Explain that, although it is legal for adults to drink alcohol, it can still be harmful. This can be supported with examples of the impact alcohol has on the body (shared in the slide deck).

nodes.misconception: Cultural exchange between Britain and India was 'one-way'.
nodes.response: Cultural exchange between Britain and India moved in both directions, with both countries being permanently changed by the other.

nodes.misconception: Incinerarting waste is good for the environment.
nodes.response: Incinerating waste releases toxic gases and carbon emissions.

nodes.misconception: Pupils assume that all volcanic eruptions cause fatalities.
nodes.response: Fatalities are reduced through detection and warning systems; evacuation procedures; emergency service response, training and funding. Iceland is very well prepared for volcanic eruptions.

nodes.misconception: Fake news is easy to spot because it’s obviously false or silly.
nodes.response: Fake news is often designed to look real and believable. It can mimic trusted sources, use partial truths, or appeal to emotions to trick people. It’s important to check information sources and think critically, even if a post seems convincing.

nodes.misconception: The British public uniformly supported imperial expansion and wars.
nodes.response: British public opinion was not monolithic; there were varied reactions to imperial policies and military actions, including support, indifference and opposition.

nodes.misconception: Network failure just means the internet stops working for a bit; it’s annoying but not serious.
nodes.response: Network failure can lead to data loss, financial damage and safety risks in sectors like healthcare. It is more than just an inconvenience and can impact lives and businesses.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that population size is only affected by the number of people being born.
nodes.response: Use the lesson resources to explain that many factors have an impact on population size, with the main contributing factor currently being the increase in life expectancy.

nodes.misconception: That being a housewife was an easy role.
nodes.response: Working in the home on domestic tasks for 70 hours a week was more than a full time working week with a paid job.

nodes.misconception: That deforestation and logging are the same thing.
nodes.response: Logging is the use of trees as a natural resource for their wood and can happen legally or illegaly. Deforestation is the cutting down of trees for many reasons, often to make space for other activities such as mining, road building or farming.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that vaping is a safe and healthy practice, or a ‘cleaner’ version of smoking.
nodes.response: Explain that, although vaping is less harmful to the body than smoking, it still has an impact on the body and, as a new practice, we are not yet fully aware of the long term effects.

nodes.misconception: There is agreement about why the USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
nodes.response: The US decision to use atomic bombs at the end of WW2 remains deeply controversial and historians disagree about the motivation with some arguing that it was to force the Japanese to surrender while others arguing it was to intimidate the USSR.

nodes.misconception: There is agreement about why the USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
nodes.response: The US decision to use atomic bombs at the end of WW2 remains deeply controversial and historians disagree about the motivation with some arguing that it was to force the Japanese to surrender while others arguing it was to intimidate the USSR.

nodes.misconception: The Black Death was a terrible one-off event.
nodes.response: Although the Black Death was a one-off event, the plague, the disease that was the Black Death, continued to afflict Europe for hundreds of years after it first came to Europe in the 14th century.

nodes.misconception: Historical events have one cause.
nodes.response: This will be addressed across the course of the unit, but within this lesson it is worth drawing attention to the competing causes listed in the discussion of the Peasants' Revolt.

nodes.misconception: Laws are regularly scrutinised and updated by the government.
nodes.response: Many laws remain unchanged and in place for an exceedingly long time. Sometimes new laws are created which make the old ones redundant, but other times there is no need to replace the existing law if it is still relevant.

nodes.misconception: The European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Union (EU) have always been the same entity with identical goals and functions.
nodes.response: The evolution from the EEC to the EU over several decades, showing progressively deepening integration. This was not a seamless transition but involved significant changes in scope and objectives.

nodes.misconception: All the Haitian rebels were enslaved people.
nodes.response: Many of the Haitian rebels were free people.

nodes.misconception: Oberon knows Titania will fall in love with Bottom.
nodes.response: Oberon hopes Titania will fall in love with something "vile" but he doesn't know about Bottom, or his transformation, until Puck tells him the joke he has played.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may consider sources to be inherently useful or not useful and make statements about bias.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that all sources are useful for investigating something, and that the questions we ask of them are important in this process.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think all Britons became pagans.
nodes.response: It is likely that some Britons adopted pagan beliefs when the Anglo-Saxons settled. Some may have continued to follow Christianity.

nodes.misconception: All kingdoms in West Africa saw the same changes as a result of the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
nodes.response: Some kingdoms were weaker as a result of wars between kingdoms, others were weakened because of alliances and others continued to thrive.

nodes.misconception: Non-white soldiers and citizens of the Commonwealth played a small role during and after both World Wars.
nodes.response: Non-white soldiers and citizens of the Commonwealth played a significant role during and after both World Wars.

nodes.misconception: The impact of WWI was limited to Europe, and those directly affected by the deaths of troops.
nodes.response: The impact of WWI can be seen in Britain across different groups in society, but also within British colonies across the world.

nodes.misconception: That sea level is constantly the same and that elevation is the same as height in general.
nodes.response: Sea level changes with the tides; the measure that we use as a baseline is the mean (average) sea level. This is used to calculate elevation of geographical features; sea level is taken as zero and every 1 metre in height is 1 metre above sea level.

nodes.misconception: Pupils can fall into the habit of writing superficial explanations or fail to extend them fully.
nodes.response: An extended explanation would be: Regeneration and rebranding in Liverpool led to economic growth as a result of more businesses and tourism. This led to more diverse jobs and has contributed to a stronger and more resilient local economy.

nodes.misconception: Geological resources are all bad because they damage the environment.
nodes.response: While they can cause environmental harm, they also provide essential materials and economic benefits. The key is understanding both advantages and disadvantages—which is what geographers evaluate.

nodes.misconception: Music and songs written a long time ago aren’t relevant to us now.
nodes.response: Music and songs from the past can help us to connect with, and better understand many people, both at home and abroad.

nodes.misconception: That you should not use your own opinions or perspectives when exploring a text.
nodes.response: Being able to articulate your own opinions and perspectives is an important skill to have. They should be rooted in evidence from the text and should avoid speculation.

nodes.misconception: Biodiversity conservation can only take place in large natural habitats such as forests.
nodes.response: Biodiversity conservation can take place on a small scale, for example, by providing habitats in gardens and in urban areas.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that villi and alveoli increase surface area without changing volume.
nodes.response: These ideas are explored in detail with examples and demonstrations using cube animals. The issue of surface area to volume ratio and diffusion rate is covered thoroughly, along with solutions to the issues in humans.

nodes.misconception: Students struggle with the idea that plants have organs and systems like humans, and that all these systems and cells are adapted with specialised features to enable them to do their job effectively.
nodes.response: The plant vascular system and human circulatory system have been compared, and human lung alveoli and digestive system villi have been compared with root hair cells.

nodes.misconception: Household chores are not examples of physical activity but sports, running and climbing are. Playing, dancing and walking are not fitness activities.
nodes.response: Examples of a variety of different physical activities.

nodes.misconception: Students thinking that certain sports only need one type of component of fitness to be successful e.g. 100m sprinter just needs speed.
nodes.response: Identify all the components of fitness that are useful for each athlete, determining why they are beneficial and justifying which is most important.

nodes.misconception: Access to electricity means 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
nodes.response: Having access to electricity means having an electricity source that can provide lighting and charge a phone or radio for 4 hours a day. In LICs, and some NEEs, electricity outages are part of daily life.

nodes.misconception: It is common for pupils to misunderstand the links between increased or decreased body temperature and the impact on enzyme function, and changes in water concentration and cell structure.
nodes.response: Explanations of the effect of temperature on enzyme activity, the link between body temperature and enzyme function, and conditions such as hyper- and hypo-thermia are made. The link between water balance, osmosis and cell shapes are also explored.

nodes.misconception: It is common for pupils to misunderstand the links between increased or decreased body temperature and the impact on enzyme function.
nodes.response: Explanations of the effect of temperature on enzyme activity, the link between body temperature and enzyme function, and conditions such as hyper- and hypo-thermia are made and explored in this lesson.

nodes.misconception: Artists always work alone to create their art.
nodes.response: Many artists collaborate with others, work in teams, or invite the community to be part of the process.

nodes.misconception: All Christians were against scientific development.
nodes.response: Within all religions (or groups in society) there will be plurality of thought, including progressive viewpoints.

nodes.misconception: Soil is just dirt.
nodes.response: Soil is a complex and vital resource made of minerals, organic matter, water, and living organisms. It is important for growing food, storing carbon, and maintaining ecosystems. Without healthy soil, agriculture and natural habitats wouldn't survive.

nodes.misconception: The kirpan is a weapon carried for violent purposes.
nodes.response: The kirpan is a ceremonial and religious article carried by initiated Khalsa Sikhs as a symbol of their duty to stand up against injustice, not to harm others. It is one of the 5 Ks that represent Sikh identity and commitment to Waheguru (God).

nodes.misconception: You can only trade goods.
nodes.response: You can trade goods and services such as education and finance services.

nodes.misconception: Only people who are religious go on pilgrimage.
nodes.response: Anyone can go on a pilgrimage, whether they are religious or not. However, most pilgrims are religious.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that Zheng He went on his voyages by himself.
nodes.response: He was admiral of the Chinese fleet. He took many ships and lots of sailors on the voyages.

nodes.misconception: India was totally controlled by the East India Company at the time of the Indian Rebellion in 1857.
nodes.response: Two-thirds of India was controlled by the East India Company at the time of the Indian Rebellion in 1857.

nodes.misconception: The Industrial Revolution affected all aspects of life in Britain equally.
nodes.response: The impact of the Industrial Revolution may be measured differently depending on which aspects of life historians focus their attention on.

nodes.misconception: The Industrial Revolution led to a decline in living conditions across all parts of Britain.
nodes.response: The decline in living conditions during the Industrial Revolution was generally confined to industrial towns and their poorest areas.

nodes.misconception: The discrimination and exclusion from opportunities that migrants sometimes face is just something these communities have to accept.
nodes.response: In fact, migrants set up self-help schemes and organise their own resources to ensure discrimination and lack of government help do not hold back their community and especially their children's access to opportunities.

nodes.misconception: Spit formation occurs solely from sediment deposition.
nodes.response: Longshore drift, wave and wind direction play an important role in the formation of spits, and a change in direction of the coastline is required.

nodes.misconception: Art movements came about in isolation from the world around them.
nodes.response: Art movements are often impacted by changes in the world around them.

nodes.misconception: Males only have Y chromosomes, only males inherit sex-linked conditions.
nodes.response: Males have one Y and one X chromosome, males only need one recessive allele to suffer from a sex-linked genetic disorder, whereas females need two and therefore the condition is less common in females.

nodes.misconception: Males only have Y chromosomes.
nodes.response: Males have one Y and one X chromosome.

nodes.misconception: The Inspector is a ghost and his supernatural qualitites should be interpreted literally.
nodes.response: Whilst this is one interpretation, it must be considered alongside the symbolic value of the Inspector’s supernatural elements and Priestley’s purpose.

nodes.misconception: Hand drum technique is the same across the world.
nodes.response: Techniques are very different on different hand drums around the world. Tabla, doumbek and djembe all use very different techniques, for example, the doumbek technique uses fingertips in a way that djembe does not.

nodes.misconception: Writing the y intercept as a single value or getting the x and y coordinates the wrong way around.
nodes.response: Encourage writing the y intercept as a coordinate. Stating 'lines cross the y axis when x=0' can help pupils write the coordinate correctly.

nodes.misconception: Litter in the nutrient cycle is considered biotic.
nodes.response: Litter in the nutrient cycle is considered abiotic because it consists of non-living organic material, such as dead leaves and decomposing matter. Although it originated from living organisms, once it becomes litter, it is classified as non-living.

nodes.misconception: Children my believe that a country's time zone is fixed and cannot be changed.
nodes.response: Countries occasionally change their time zone for practical or political reasons. For example, in 2024, Kazakhstan moved from using two time zones to observing only one times zone across the whole country: UTC+5

nodes.misconception: The internet and WWW are just different words used to decribe the same thing.
nodes.response: The World Wide Web is a service that runs on the internet. The internet is a network that allows computers to communicate and provide the means for computers to uses services such as the WWW.

nodes.misconception: The internet is the same as the World Wide Web.
nodes.response: The World Wide Web is a service that is offered over the internet. The internet is the network that transfers data whilst the World Wide Web is the system of sharing information that people use.

nodes.misconception: Singing a melody is only possible if you are a very strong singer.
nodes.response: Everyone can sing, but keeping to a small range of notes can help when building confidence with singing. Singing helps us to internalise the notes and really 'feel' the melody. Melodies can sound much more natural when sung.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may assume that people have always been able to take photographs.
nodes.response: Explain that photography was invented 200 years ago and, before that, photographs did not exist. People would have drawn or painted to record what they could see in front of them.

nodes.misconception: A positive correlation means one variable has an impact on another.
nodes.response: Just because there is a correlation, it doesn’t necessarily mean that one things causes another to increase.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that because Renaissance architects used mathematical calculations to design their buildings, these were without subsequent problems or issues.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that these architects often made miscalculations and many subsequent improvement works were needed to ensure buildings like St Peter's did not fall down.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that because printing presses were mechanical, they were as fast and efficient as modern machinery.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that even though printing presses were much quicker than copying by hand, it could still take a relatively long time to print books.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that dissection was banned by the medieval Catholic Church.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that, while dissection was not banned, there was still a taboo around handling dead bodies which limited the number of dissections that took place during the medieval period.

nodes.misconception: Children may be using 'ge' and 'dge' interchangeably.
nodes.response: Be very explicit about 'dge' being found alongside the short vowel and the 'ge' spelling being found alongside other vowel sounds.

nodes.misconception: US presidents would only use federal intervention when pressured by the media.
nodes.response: Kennedy marked a change in the involvement of the president, as he was not pressured by the media to use federal intervention to support Meredith. Unlike in Little Rock, Kennedy's support came before the outbreak of violence from white Americans.

nodes.misconception: Jewish festivals are always celebrated in the synagogue.
nodes.response: Sukkot is celebrated in the garden.

nodes.misconception: The covenant is ancient and has no meaning for today.
nodes.response: Jews today still remember the covenant with Abraham.

nodes.misconception: Any war fought by Christians is automatically 'just'.
nodes.response: The Just War theory has strict rules that many wars don’t meet. Some students may think wars like WWI or the Crusades were 'just' because Christians fought in them, without realising conditions like the last resort or proportionality weren’t met.

nodes.misconception: Musical genres have rules to follow, and styles never mix or borrow ideas from each other.
nodes.response: Like the rainbow, music is a continuing spectrum of ideas, with genres of blending and merging into each other, borrowing, sharing and adapting key features and ideas.

nodes.misconception: The movements and shouts are not related to the pulse and rhythm.
nodes.response: The movements and shouts, just like the drum strikes, are rhythmically important. Reinforce the pulse when teaching the movements, shouts and strikes.

nodes.misconception: The controversies and conflicts between the crown and the Church were specific to Norman England.
nodes.response: In fact, the controversies and conflicts between the Church and the crown happened in many kingdoms in Europe, and were more severe than in England in particular cases, especially the Holy Roman Empire.

nodes.misconception: European merchants arrived in West Africa with the intention of starting to enslave people.
nodes.response: European merchants were attracted by the potential amount of gold they would be able to trade in West Africa.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may confuse the 'al' and 'il' spellings with other similar-sounding endings or 'l' spellings.
nodes.response: Be explicit about the irregularities and exceptions in English and use phonics, word games and pattern spotting to reinforce spellings.

nodes.misconception: Children may think that the vowel sound preceding the 'l' will always determine the spelling.
nodes.response: Showing examples of incorrect use of 'el' and 'le' alongside the correct can be very useful for children to spot the correct spelling.

nodes.misconception: The Lady of Shalott chooses to take her own life on the way to Camelot.
nodes.response: The Lady of Shalott realises that, because she got up from her loom, she is now cursed. Knowing she will die from this curse, she gets into the boat to sail to Camelot. She realises she will not make it there alive.

nodes.misconception: Children may think the mountains of the Lake District are volcanoes.
nodes.response: The volcanoes which produces the lava and ash that fell onto the Lake District were not the mountains themselves. Volcanic rock formed as a result of nearby volcanic activity.

nodes.misconception: Weaving is simply a way of creating fabric for clothing and has no connection to storytelling or culture.
nodes.response: Weaving goes beyond just making fabric; it’s a powerful form of art that can tell stories and reflect cultural heritage.

nodes.misconception: Most Muslims believe in the immortality of the soul but not the body.
nodes.response: The majority of Muslims believe in a physical resurrection.

nodes.misconception: Jesus did not suffer during his crucifixion.
nodes.response: The Gospels recall Jesus crying out loudly during his crucifixion, which many Christians interpret as a sign of Jesus' pain.

nodes.misconception: The atomic bombs dropped on Japan only had immediate impacts.
nodes.response: The bombs had unprecedented destructive power. They sent out a shock wave that incinerated everything within a four-mile radius and in the weeks that followed, people died from radiation poisoning despite having survived the initial blast.

nodes.misconception: Jesus was a Christian.
nodes.response: Jesus was a Jew and followed Jewish traditions. Jesus celebrated the Pesach meal with his disciples.

nodes.misconception: When dividing terms with coefficients, pupils also subtract the coefficients as well as the exponents.
nodes.response: Pupils should be encouraged to rewrite their expression as a fraction, with the number parts grouped and powers grouped. This hopefully avoids this error as they can see the fraction line as a division.

nodes.misconception: Pupils multiply the base by the fractional exponent. e.g 25^(1/2) = 12.5
nodes.response: The use of a calculator allows pupils to see the index of a fraction is not to be multiplied by the base. Embedding the laws of indices where two bases are the same and each number has an index of 1/2 helps recognize the 1/2 index as a square root.

nodes.misconception: When multiplying terms with coefficients, pupils also add the coefficients as well as the exponents.
nodes.response: Pupils should be encouraged to rewrite their expression using the associative and commutative laws, with the number parts grouped and powers grouped.  This hopefully avoids this error as they can see it is the product of the numbers.

nodes.misconception: Any number with an index of 0 equates to 0
nodes.response: Reiterate the division of any number by itself is 1. This applies with laws of indices too. E.g 8^4 / 8^4 = 8^0. Any number divided by itself gives 1, therefore 8^0 = 1. For more advanced understanding, algebraic can be used instead of numbers.

nodes.misconception: Forgetting to raise the coefficient to the power as well as the power term.
nodes.response: Highlight that everything in the bracket is being affected by the power.  By showing examples where the bracket is written in expanded form and then the repeated multiplication helps with this.

nodes.misconception: That there are clear distinctions between good leaders and bad leaders in 'Animal Farm'.
nodes.response: Although 'Animal Farm' is simply written, its messages are complex. What is Orwell wanting to reveal about leadership in general?

nodes.misconception: That people spoke a totally different language in Ancient Greece than they speak today in modern Greece.
nodes.response: The Greek alphabet has been in use for more than 2,000 years; the same alphabet that was used in Ancient Greece is used in Greece today. Much of the Greek language stems from or is the same as Ancient Greek.

nodes.misconception: William the Conqueror was hostile towards all Anglo-Saxons from the start.
nodes.response: Some Anglo-Saxons, if they had not fought against William at Hastings, were allowed to keep their land.

nodes.misconception: Sikhs believe prayer is more important than practical service.
nodes.response: Practical, selfless service (sewa) is an essential part of being a Sikh.

nodes.misconception: Surnames have always been used and they generally aren't changed from one generation to the next.
nodes.response: During the medieval period, people went by their first name and one or more given names. These given names could be nicknames based on their place of origin or occupation or a distinguishing feature. Some people chose their own given names.

nodes.misconception: The Church is the Christian place of worship.
nodes.response: Church with a capital "C" refers to the community of Christian believers, and church with a lower case "c" refers to the Christian place of worship and often local churches and their congregations.

nodes.misconception: That Africa is a country not a geographically diverse continent.
nodes.response: Recap the names of the seven continents and five oceans. Spend more time using a map to identify different countries in Africa.

nodes.misconception: Earthquakes only occur at tectonic plate boundaries.
nodes.response: Earthquakes can occur anywhere in the world, but they are most commonly found at tectonic plate boundaries.

nodes.misconception: There is only one version of the Lord's Prayer.
nodes.response: The Lord's Prayer is said in many different churches, at home and even in some schools. It has many translations from the original language, so can sound very different.

nodes.misconception: US responses to the 'loss' of China were only based on international concerns.
nodes.response: As a democracy, American policy-makers and leaders had to pay attention to domestic opinion as well as international issues. Both of these factors encouraged tough anti-communism after the 'loss' of China.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may confuse the fairy tale and the nursery rhyme which both have the same name.
nodes.response: Use this as an opportunity to discuss the differences between fairy tales and nursery rhymes. Emphasise that most nursery rhymes include rhyme and repetition and this makes it different to the fairy tale.

nodes.misconception: Oberon and Puck deliberately try and create disorder between Hermia, Lysander, Helena and Demetrius.
nodes.response: Oberon orders Puck to put the magical potion on Demetrius so that he falls in love with Helena. Puck makes a genuine mistake by putting it on Lysander.

nodes.misconception: The magnetic field is only at the poles of a magnet.
nodes.response: Provide opportunities for pupils to plot magnetic field lines around a bar magnet and to experiment with a second magnet, as described in the teacher tip.

nodes.misconception: Students might fail to see the significance of the admission by the police that they acted with racist prejudice.
nodes.response: This was the first time the police had admitted to treating the black community unfairly and was a turning point in the development of civil rights.

nodes.misconception: That only the women in Act 1 consider marriage almost like a business transaction.
nodes.response: What does Gilbert gain from his marriage to Hortense? How does he describe his feelings towards Hortense and what does this tell the audience?

nodes.misconception: Forgiveness means forgetting what someone did or pretending it was okay.
nodes.response: In Christianity, forgiveness doesn’t mean saying the wrong didn’t happen. It means choosing to let go of anger or the need for revenge.

nodes.misconception: Tidal volume is the amount of air breathed in and out per breath and the lungs completely empty of air when we expire.
nodes.response: Tidal volume is the volume of air breathed in or out per breadth and it increases during exercise to enable more air and hence exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide to occur. A residual volume of air always remains in the lungs to keep them inflated.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that media coverage is always beneficial for sports, without considering potential negative effects and assuming that media only affects athletes and fans.
nodes.response: Media coverage can be both positive and negative and can impact performers, sports, officials, spectators and the sport itself.

nodes.misconception: Tourism at the Mer de Glace only has negative impacts.
nodes.response: Tourism at the Mer de Glace has both positive and negative impacts. Positive impacts include boosts to the local economy and an awareness of climate change.

nodes.misconception: You must write a new program every time you use the micro:bit.
nodes.response: You can reuse and edit programs on the micro:bit once they're transferred.

nodes.misconception: Levees are man made.
nodes.response: Levees can be built as a flood defence but they can also be created naturally.

nodes.misconception: Modern technology has improved individuals' working lives in all aspects.
nodes.response: There are some negative impacts of modern-day technology on the workplace and individual workers. These include fewer opportunities for face-to-face communication and 24/7 connectivity.

nodes.misconception: The number one mole represents can be difficult for pupils to grasp and appreciate.
nodes.response: Show many real world examples of 6.02 × 10²³ examples of something - that many basketballs would form a planet the size of the Earth.

nodes.misconception: The number one mole represents can be difficult for pupils to grasp and appreciate.
nodes.response: Show many real world examples of 6.02 × 10²³ examples of something - that many basketballs would form a planet the size of the Earth.

nodes.misconception: The Montgomery Bus Boycott was a successful, peaceful boycott that was carried out with minimal resistance.
nodes.response: The boycott was a peaceful means of protest, but continued despite huge resistance throughout Montgomery. Those who participated risked arrest, unemployed and sometimes their lives.

nodes.misconception: That there is categorically one thing that can be considered the most significant legacy.
nodes.response: Significance differs according to perspective and context. Something that is of great significance to one person may be of little significance to another, it all depends on the criteria that it is being judged against.

nodes.misconception: It is not clear how the magnetic field around a conducting wire interacts with a uniform magnetic field.
nodes.response: Focus on observing and predicting the direction that a conducting wire is forced in by a uniform magnetic field, and openly admit that explaining this in terms of how the magnetic field interact is too challenging to include in the syllabus.

nodes.misconception: All Hindus think this story literally happened.
nodes.response: Many Hindus will see stories such as this as helping to explain mysteries of the universe. It is not important whether the story actually happened. What is important is what the story says about humans, the universe and God.

nodes.misconception: South America and the South American plate are the same thing.
nodes.response: South America is a continent (land), whereas the South American plate also includes part of the Atlantic ocean.

nodes.misconception: Pupils will think that the Moon actually does change shape, or that it becomes covered with clouds.
nodes.response: Pupils should use models to see and feel for themselves what is actually moving and how this affects the apparent shape of the Moon.

nodes.misconception: Earth lies at the centre of the solar system, with the Sun and planets orbiting around it.
nodes.response: Provide opportunities for the children to explore both diagrams and 3D models of the solar system which clearly show the Sun and planets.

nodes.misconception: Expansion of an empire always means that is growing stronger.
nodes.response: As the Mughal Empire expanded, the costs of maintaining its rule across India also increased and new tensions were created with groups who lost out from extended Mughal control.

nodes.misconception: The murder of Thomas Becket was the undoing of Henry II.
nodes.response: Long-term it increased Henry’s control over the Church. Bishops’ opposition decreased, while the Pope gave support after 1172.

nodes.misconception: Prison chaplains just lead services and prayers.
nodes.response: Prison chaplains provide pastoral care, support rehabilitation and emotional wellbeing, help with faith-based education and often work with other organisations to support resettlement and reintegration. They also assist prisoners of all or no faiths.

nodes.misconception: The voltage (drop) across power lines is the same as the voltage they transmit.
nodes.response: Spend time to clarify that the power transmitted depends on the p.d. between the live and neutral wires, and power dissipated depends on the drop in voltage from one end of a live wire to the other.

nodes.misconception: The story of Jesus' birth appears in all four of the Gospels.
nodes.response: The story of Jesus' birth is only in the Gospels of Matthew and Luke.

nodes.misconception: All Buddhist places of worship have the same features and purpose.
nodes.response: Buddhist places of worship differ in appearance, size and function. This is often dependent on the location and which school of Buddhism it belongs to.

nodes.misconception: Marriage laws around the world are the same as England & Wales.
nodes.response: Marriage laws vary around the world including minimum age, how many spouses you can have at once, who you can marry and how marriage ceremonies are carried out.

nodes.misconception: That Sunni Muslims do not believe in the justice of Allah (Adalat) because it is not mentioned in the six articles of faith.
nodes.response: Al Adl (the just) is one of the 99 names of Allah and is important to Sunni Muslims as well as Shia but it isn't in the six articles of faith and may be seen as part of a believe in Tawhid - the oneness of God.

nodes.misconception: There is an ideal family type.
nodes.response: People may have different views on the best types but there is no ideal. All families are different.

nodes.misconception: Each quality or characteristic of God is distinct and separate from the others.
nodes.response: God's qualities and characteristics complement each other. For example, many Christians believe that God exerts his omnipotence with love for humanity, which links to God as (omni)benevolent.

nodes.misconception: If humans are capable of moral evil, it means they are inherently evil.
nodes.response: Being capable of moral evil doesn’t mean humans are inherently evil; it suggests that humans have free will and the ability to choose both good and bad actions, depending on circumstances and influences.

nodes.misconception: That Muslims believe Muhammad was the first prophet of Islam.
nodes.response: Muslims belive that Adam was the first prophet of Islam and Muhammad was the final prophet.

nodes.misconception: Students may believe Germany fully mobilised its population, including women, like the Allies did.
nodes.response: Nazi ideology restricted women's roles in industry, despite labour shortages.

nodes.misconception: All religious leaders opposed the Nazis.
nodes.response: In reality, many remained silent or even cooperated, hoping to protect their institutions.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may assume that all concentration camps in this period were death camps like Auschwitz.
nodes.response: Emphasise that early camps (1933–1939) were brutal prisons for political opponents and ‘undesirables’, but were not yet part of a systematic extermination programme. The Holocaust’s industrial death camps came later.

nodes.misconception: Compression is only useful for pictures or photos.
nodes.response: Compression applies to many types of files such as MP3 for audio, MP4 for video, ZIP for grouped files.

nodes.misconception: All Abrahamic religions believe that Jesus is the New covenant.
nodes.response: Jesus as the New covenant is central to Christian belief. Most Jews do not believe that Jesus is the New covenant. In Islam, Jesus is considered a prophet.

nodes.misconception: Every element of the NHS was free for a considerable time after its creation.
nodes.response: Every element of the NHS was only free for a short time, as the overwhelming demand resulted in the need to introduce prescription fees.

nodes.misconception: Inequality is just about the difference in how much money people have.
nodes.response: There are many different inequalities in people's lives. Other inequalities include access to education and healthcare, job opportunities, access to technology and how people are treated.

nodes.misconception: England’s monarchs always spoke English as their first language.
nodes.response: In fact, after the Norman conquest it would take over 300 years for the monarch of England to speak English as their first language.

nodes.misconception: The Norman conquest was a brutal military occupation which resulted in wholescale change of the English Church.
nodes.response: Whilst there were significant changes, the English Church retained its basic structure and liturgy.

nodes.misconception: England had not been invaded before the Norman Conquest.
nodes.response: Britain had been invaded many times before the Norman Conquest: by the Romans, the tribes known as Angles and Saxons and by the Vikings.

nodes.misconception: Paying homage, swearing allegiance, or making promises were weak obligations.
nodes.response: In fact, these promises are with the king and God. It was unlikely you would break a public and spiritual promise like this; it would not have been good for your reputation or your soul!

nodes.misconception: The Arctic is just at the North Pole.
nodes.response: The Arctic is all the area within the Arctic circle, which includes parts of Europe, North America and Asia.

nodes.misconception: Everyone living in a particular region will have a similar lived experience of a place.
nodes.response: Though in general the north and south of the UK show evidence of economic inequality, there are lots of pockets of very high levels of wealth in the north and areas of extreme poverty in the south.

nodes.misconception: William always used violence to control England.
nodes.response: Although violence was a recurring tactic of William's, he also allowed some Anglo-Saxons to keep some of their land and was willing to negotiate and pay the Danes to leave England.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that we can learn little from imagery that has been produced for the purposes of propaganda.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that we can learn a lot from such imagery as it is a window into the minds of those who had it produced, and helps us to understand some of their concerns and motivations.

nodes.misconception: Everybody agreed the possession of nuclear weapons made the world more dangerous.
nodes.response: Many people argued that as the US and USSR both possessed nuclear weapons this deterred them from going to war with one another - otherwise they woudl afce mutually assured destruction.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may read the 'ow' in words such as 'below' and 'snow' as an 'ou' sound, such as in 'growl'.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that when the 'ow' digraph appears at the end of the word, it is typically making an 'oa' sound.

nodes.misconception: All Obas of Benin were male.
nodes.response: While historically most Obas were, indeed, male, there were exceptions, and a few female rulers, known as "Queen Mothers," held significant influence and power. The Queen Mothers often acted as regents for young kings or played advisory roles.

nodes.misconception: A humanist belief in the one life means that they can do whatever they want.
nodes.response: A humanist belief in the one life motivates them to find meaning, purpose and happiness.

nodes.misconception: Confusion of 'now'/'know' and 'new'/'knew'. 'Ow' can be pronounced in different ways.
nodes.response: Teach examples of silent letters explicitly and get children to keep an eye out for them in their wider reading.

nodes.misconception: The first scene is an exciting spectacle but not important to the rest of the play.
nodes.response: Despite its length, this scene grounds us in the atmosphere and main themes of the play.

nodes.misconception: The operating system is just what you see on the screen.
nodes.response: What you see on the screen is the graphical interface, but the operating system includes a lot more behind the scenes such as memory management, file systems, device control etc.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may conflate cyclic quadrilaterals with cases of "the angle at the centre of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference" theorem, when the angle at the centre is a reflex angle.
nodes.response: While the two diagrams may look similar at a glance, pay extra attention to whether all four points of the quadrilateral are on the circumference or if one of the points is in the centre.

nodes.misconception: Pupils can think the 'rules' for the spelling will always help to choose the right spelling.
nodes.response: Explain that rules can help us a certain amount.  We also need to use our judgement of 'what looks right'.

nodes.misconception: The orchestra has only grown through the adding of more of the same instruments.
nodes.response: The number of players has increased, but the variety of instruments has also increased. Many different instruments have been added to the orchestra since the 1600s, including brass, woodwind, percussion and keyboard instruments.

nodes.misconception: The Punjab is part of India.
nodes.response: The Punjab is an area split between modern-day India and Pakistan. It has a distinct history, culture and traditions as a region, one of which is bhangra.

nodes.misconception: The British were the only European power trying to gain control over India.
nodes.response: The British, French and Dutch were all attempting to gain a foothold in India and expand their influence there.

nodes.misconception: Blues is an old style of music that isn't relevant anymore.
nodes.response: While it's true that blues first developed more than a century ago, it continued to be an important style all through the 20th century and up to the present day. It shaped many different styles (including rock) that came to be incredibly important.

nodes.misconception: Because rock 'n' roll often uses the 12-bar blues, this means it is just a type of blues.
nodes.response: Many styles use the 12-bar blues, including pop, rock, jazz and other styles. While rock 'n' roll is closely related to blues, its defining features are quite different, and its role as a commerical pop style is far from the origins of blues.

nodes.misconception: Historians agree that the Cold War started in 1945 with the end of World War Two.
nodes.response: The breakdown of the wartime alliance and the emerging ideological rift between communism and capitalism unfolded over several years. The exact start date of the Cold War is often debated among historians.

nodes.misconception: Historians agree that the Cold War started in 1945 with the end of World War Two.
nodes.response: The breakdown of the wartime alliance and the emerging ideological rift between communism and capitalism unfolded over several years. The exact start date of the Cold War is often debated among historians.

nodes.misconception: Only British people fought for Britain during the Second World War.
nodes.response: Highlight how millions of men and women from around the world helped the British armed forces.

nodes.misconception: That the assassination of Ferdinand led to the inevitable, immediate outbreak of a global war
nodes.response: The outbreak of the war was the result of a series of context-dependent events, including the Austrian ultimatum and the Schlieffen Plan

nodes.misconception: That symbols in literature mean the same to everyone.
nodes.response: Our responses to symbolism depend on our experiences as well as exposure to certain concepts so we might all have very different responses.

nodes.misconception: Boycotting palm oil helps stop deforestation.
nodes.response: Experts recommend supporting certified sustainable palm oil, as palm oil is the most land-efficient oil crop. Replacing it with less efficient crops like sunflowers could cause more deforestation.

nodes.misconception: The Parable of the Good Samaritan is simply about kindness.
nodes.response: The Parable of the Good Samaritan answers the question, ‘who is my neighbour?’ in a radical way. Jesus has the hero of the story as someone who his audience would have considered unclean and would have been shunned by most people.

nodes.misconception: The only point of the parable is welcoming home the lost son.
nodes.response: The parable is about the father’s love and forgiveness for both his sons.

nodes.misconception: The US has always been too large and powerful to lose a war.
nodes.response: The majority of people regard the Vietnam War as a loss for the US: they did not achieve their stated goal of containing communism.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often think that the particles are embedded in the substance rather than being the substance. Most pupils think that substances in the liquid state will compress a little.
nodes.response: Reinforce that most substances can exist in all three states of matter and when they are in the gas state there is nothing between the particles but empty space.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think the function of flowers is to make plants look nice or that they are there for the benefit of humans.
nodes.response: Explain that flowers are the reproductive parts of a plant that allow it to make more seeds.

nodes.misconception: The role of the stomach is often misunderstood as the main or only place where digestion occurs.
nodes.response: The lesson explores the roles of the stomach and the intestines in digesting food and absorbing nutrients.

nodes.misconception: In Spanish, all adjectives go after the noun.
nodes.response: Most Spanish adjectives go after the noun; they describe objective qualities (traits, origin, colours,...). However, some adjectives go before the noun; these prenominal adjectives often express subjective opinions or give emphasis.

nodes.misconception: Titania seems to have some power, but Hermia has none.
nodes.response: Hermia defies her father by saying that she will marry Lysander, and refusing to marry Demetrius. She is also willing to leave her father, and the place she was born rather than obey her father.

nodes.misconception: After Martin Luther King's famous 'I have a dream' speech, the civil rights movement continued to progress until the Civil Rights Act was passed.
nodes.response: The assassination of President Kennedy stalled the momentum the movement had gained with the events in Birmingham, he was the president that many black American had put their hope in - and many feared their hope died with him.

nodes.misconception: Revolts and rebellions are driven purely by rage and frustration.
nodes.response: Most revolts and rebellions have a number of causes and are usually led by people with a plan and aims to achieve.

nodes.misconception: Mistaking another note for F when changing position quickly. The timpani are untuned percussion because they are drums.
nodes.response: Reinforce that F is to the left of the three black keys. Highlight that the timpani are tuned to specific pitches.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may assume that a radius which intersects a chord always bisects the chord.
nodes.response: A radius only bisects a chord if they are perpendicular.

nodes.misconception: Hitler invented antisemitism.
nodes.response: Antisemitism had deep roots across Europe and the wider world long before Hitler. The Nazis built on these longstanding prejudices, turning them into official state policy and using them to justify persecution.

nodes.misconception: That the historical places named still exist today.
nodes.response: Over time, names and boundaries of places can change. Some places cease to exist entirely while the locations of some places do still exist but they have a different name today. A large area of Persia for example is in the modern-day country of Iran.

nodes.misconception: In French, like in English, there is only one way to say 'the'.
nodes.response: There is more than one word to say 'the' in French. For singular masculine nouns, use 'le', and for singular feminine nouns, use 'la'.

nodes.misconception: Like Hobbes, Rousseau saw the 'state of nature' as meaning without society, humans live in fear and conflict.
nodes.response: Rousseau's view contrasts directly with Hobbes', he described the state of nature as a time when humans were free, equal, and lived harmoniously, not chaotic or lawless.

nodes.misconception: Hobbes rejected all religious beliefs.
nodes.response: Hobbes did not reject religion outright. Instead, he argued that religious interpretations and practices should be subject to the authority of the sovereign for the sake of social order.

nodes.misconception: Piano concertos are just the same as other concertos.
nodes.response: Not quite. Because of the unique abilities of the piano - including its range and ability to play multiple lines at once - composers use it slightly differently to other instruments. This includes using it to accompany itself, or the orchestra.

nodes.misconception: That Napoleon and Old Major are completely different.
nodes.response: Look closely at their speeches. Interestingly they are very similar in their uses of devices, delivery and how they motivate the animals.

nodes.misconception: The Commonwealth represents nothing more than a cultural and historical connection between countries.
nodes.response: Commonwealth states meet every two years to promote trade relationships, human rights and development aid.

nodes.misconception: Earth lies at the centre of our solar system, with the Sun and planets orbiting around it.
nodes.response: Provide opportunities for the children to explore both diagrams and 3D models of the solar system which clearly show the Sun and planets.

nodes.misconception: EIC victory in the Battle of Plassey only relied upon its own strengths.
nodes.response: The EIC army benefitted from Indian support, including its secret agreement with Mir Jafar who refused to let his troops participate in the battle.

nodes.misconception: The magical potion is removed from everyone's eyes at the end of the play.
nodes.response: Demetrius still has the magical potion on his eyes. This is why he is in love with Helena.

nodes.misconception: Martin Luther King initiated the Protestant Reformation.
nodes.response: Martin Luther, a German monk and theologian, initiated the Protestant Reformation in the 1500s. Martin Luther King was a minister and social rights activist in America in the 1900s. They are two different people.

nodes.misconception: Population density is the same everywhere in India.
nodes.response: Population density varies across India; urban areas are densely populated, but rural areas, such as much of the Himalayas, are sparsely populated.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often get the command language of describe and explain mixed up, most often causing them to explain something when just a description has been asked for.
nodes.response: A description gives details of what something is like. It should contain as much detail as possible. An explanation gives reasons for the features and should use langauge such as 'because', 'as a result of', 'due to'.

nodes.misconception: Population density is the same across the UK.
nodes.response: Population density varies widely due to factors like topography and urbanisation.

nodes.misconception: Children may think that a shadow is cast in between the object and the light source.
nodes.response: Children need to explore shadows cast by different light sources in different positions and with different objects. They should note the position of the light source in relation to the object and the shadow each time.

nodes.misconception: All electrical appliances and circuits use the same type of switch.
nodes.response: Pupils will be introduced to a wide range of switches.

nodes.misconception: Victorian women played no political role in Britain in the 19th century.
nodes.response: Women were increasingly politically active in Britain, for example, through their involvement in the abolitionist movement and through their participation in trade unions, despite being unable to vote.

nodes.misconception: Research is not a form of industry because it does not involve trade.
nodes.response: Research is an industry because it creates wealth through innovation and knowledge which has value.

nodes.misconception: Pupils do not appreciate the extent of Frankenstein's immorality.
nodes.response: In pursuit of knowledge, Frankenstein broke natural and political laws. He robbed graves and tortured live animals to achieve his ambition.

nodes.misconception: "You" is the only form of direct address when addressing a reader/audience.
nodes.response: When teaching the over reliance on direct address, rapidly fire questions to one pupil, addressing them as 'you'. Ask them how this feels.

nodes.misconception: Singing in groups is no different to singing by yourself.
nodes.response: Research shows that the positive effects of singing are even greater in larger groups.  This is partly because of the additional benefit of a shared emotion, and social bonding.

nodes.misconception: Alexander Dubcek was not a committed communist.
nodes.response: Dubcek was a committed communist. The purpose of the Prague Spring reforms was to preserve communist rule in Czechoslovakia and win support for communism by removing its worst features (e.g., censorship, secret police etc.)

nodes.misconception: Dubček's reforms demonstrate that he was not a communist.
nodes.response: Dubček did want to liberalise politics and the economy in Czechoslovakia but he was still a communist. He considered these reforms necessary to ensure that a communist government could survive without being overthrown.

nodes.misconception: Artists inspired by nature can only look carefully at natural forms and record them.
nodes.response: Artists can make art in and with nature as well as recording from nature.

nodes.misconception: Viv, Del and Enid are not British citizens.
nodes.response: All three women are British citizens. Enid relocated from one part of the Commonwealth to another. During this post war period, this ensured legal status in Britain. Viv and Del were born in Britain.

nodes.misconception: The characters in 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' are Elizabethan.
nodes.response: The play's first audiences were Elizabethan, and Shakespeare explores Elizabethan attitudes and ideas in the play. But the play is set in Athens many centuries before the Elizabethan period.

nodes.misconception: Students have a tendency to view Ralph as a morally-virtuous character who does no wrong.
nodes.response: Ralph does behave immorally and wickedly in the text - he is mean to Piggy about his asthma and he participates in the murder of Simon. What separates Ralph from the others is the remorse he shows for his actions and how he learns from them.

nodes.misconception: 'Leave Taking' is a commentary on the experiences of all women.
nodes.response: Pinnock presents the unique stories of her created characters. The centrality of women suggests she is making some sort of social comment, but she is not generalising about every single woman's experience of the world.

nodes.misconception: Overload is negative and should not be encouraged during training.
nodes.response: Overload is encouarged as a positive aspect of traning as progression is being managed correctly to bring about adaptations to fitness. It is not to be confused with 'overtraining' which can cause injuries.

nodes.misconception: Once ink is applied to the plate, the design is fixed and cannot be changed.
nodes.response: The printing process is about trying and adjusting. Artists can refine their design through trial and error, removing layers of ink or adding new ones to adjust their composition. It’s important to approach the process with flexibility and patience.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that 'likely' from the scale of likelihoods is only equal to a specific probability (e.g. 75%).
nodes.response: All probabilities that are greater than 50% but less than 100% are equivalent to 'likely' on the scale of likelihoods.

nodes.misconception: Christians ignore the problem of evil and suffering.
nodes.response: Many Christians recognise the problem of evil and suffering in the world, and in their own lives, and respond to the problem by referring to teachings from the Bible.

nodes.misconception: The existence of evil and suffering proves that God does not exist.
nodes.response: For Christians, there are a number of Biblical, theoretical and practical responses and solutions to the problem of evil.

nodes.misconception: The government is there to help people when they are in need.
nodes.response: Throughout much of history, governments have regularly failed to support the most vulnerable in society, as many of them did not see that as their function.

nodes.misconception: The CPU is the brain of the computer and understands the instructions received.
nodes.response: The CPU is the core of the computer system and receives instructions that it then executes with the help of the different components.

nodes.misconception: The first two binomials have to be multiplied first.
nodes.response: Look for features of the binomials that suggest which binomials will be easiest to multiply first. Any order will give the same final product but a particular order may reduce complexity.

nodes.misconception: Missing out partial products
nodes.response: Relating back to numerical examples and showing that 12 × 34 is not just 10 × 30 + 2 × 4. Using algebra tiles and area models can help to support student's understanding.

nodes.misconception: You don't need to consider the inputs, outputs and processes of a program during the analysis stage.
nodes.response: Listing the inputs, processes and outputs before coding helps you clearly understand what the program needs to do, avoid mistakes and save time later. It breaks the problem into smaller steps, making it easier to solve and explain to others.

nodes.misconception: The promised lands are only significant within Judaism.
nodes.response: The promised lands are significant for different reasons within the three Abrahamic religions.

nodes.misconception: Christians think that families are only important for procreation.
nodes.response: Some Christians emphasise that families are important for procreation, but this is not the only purpose of families.

nodes.misconception: The Weimar Republic’s reliance on the Freikorps might suggest that the government supported right-wing ideologies.
nodes.response: The Weimar Government used the Freikorps out of desperation to suppress left-wing uprisings, but this reliance highlighted its inability to maintain order independently, rather than an alignment with right-wing ideologies.

nodes.misconception: All textiles are fabric.
nodes.response: Remind children that fabric is one kind of textile. There are many different kinds of textiles including felted materials, waterproof materials and synthetic fibers.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think the race is about placing and running in the fastest time.
nodes.response: Yes placings are given, but the key focus is to complete the race in a time that you know is representative of you working to the best of your ability.

nodes.misconception: The story of Rama and Sita is simply about light overcoming darkness.
nodes.response: The Ramayana has many deeper meanings. At its heart is the concept of dharma, and many Hindus look to the text and its characters as role models and for guidance in life.

nodes.misconception: To calculate the instantaneous rate of reaction by reading values from the graph at a specific time.
nodes.response: Students need to draw a tangent in order to calculate the gradient of the graph at a specific time to work out the instantaneous rate of reaction.

nodes.misconception: The reactant disappears during the reaction. Acids and metals react because the acid eats away the metal.
nodes.response: Use word and symbol equations to reinforce the idea that during the reaction new chemicals are produced from the reactants. Demonstrate that metals less reactive than hydrogen will not react with acid.

nodes.misconception: The Windrush generation entered Britain illegally.
nodes.response: Those coming from the British Commonwealth were considered citizens. Migrants like Hortense and Gilbert were actively encouraged to believe that Britain was their 'home'.

nodes.misconception: The USSR was in favout of the US decision to improve relations with communist China.
nodes.response: Because of the Sino-Soviet split, the Soviets worried that improved US-China relations might lead them to form an anti-Soviet alliance.

nodes.misconception: The Normans reforms of the Church were specific to England.
nodes.response: The Church reforms were part of a much bigger European reform movement led by a succession of popes known as the Reform Papacy.

nodes.misconception: The Enabling Act was passed fairly.
nodes.response: The vote was deeply manipulated: communist Reichstag members were banned, others intimidated.

nodes.misconception: Napoleon became Emperor of France after he seized power from the Directory in 1799.
nodes.response: Napoleon became First Consul after seizing power from the Directory, but did not crown himself Emperor of France until 1804.

nodes.misconception: Thinking that being physically fit means someone is automatically healthy.
nodes.response: Explain that just because someone appears physically fit doesn't mean they have good emotional or social health.

nodes.misconception: Thinking that being physically fit means someone is automatically healthy.
nodes.response: Explain that just because someone is appears physically fit doesn't mean they may have good emotional or social health.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often draw heart rate down to zero on a line graph.
nodes.response: Even at rest your heart is still beating, on average 72 beats per minute, to ensure blood is always circulating around the body to keep you alive.

nodes.misconception: There is just one reason that Macbeth doesn't want to commit regicide - his loyalty to Duncan.
nodes.response: Macbeth's soliloquy explores crime but significantly earthly punishment. For Macbeth, the consequence on earth is what frightens him.

nodes.misconception: Children may struggle to make the connection between multiplying by 0.01 and dividing by 100
nodes.response: When we multiply by 0.01, it is the same as multiplying by one-hundredth. When we multiply by a unit fraction, we can divide by the denominator - in this case, 100

nodes.misconception: Children may struggle to make the connection between multiplying by 0.1 and dividing by ten.
nodes.response: When we multiply by 0.1, it is the same as multiplying by one-tenth. When we multiply by a unit fraction, we can divide by the denominator - in this case, 10.

nodes.misconception: Christianity and evolution are completely incompatible.
nodes.response: Many Christian denominations accept evolution as part of God's creative process, including the Catholic Church and the Church of England.

nodes.misconception: The Church of England and the Anglican Church are separate.
nodes.response: The Anglican Church originates from the Church of England. 'Anglican' is the term for Churches all over the world that are rooted in the beliefs, teachings and practices of the Church of England. The Church of England is also referred to as Anglican.

nodes.misconception: The Earth, Sun and Moon are the same size, or that the Sun is much smaller than it actually is.
nodes.response: Provide opportunities for children to explore diagrams and 3D models of the Earth, Sun and Moon which clearly show the differences in size.

nodes.misconception: Mixing up a prediction, an observation and an explanation.
nodes.response: This practical lesson explores predictions, observations and explanations in the context of using iodine solution to test leaves for starch.

nodes.misconception: The White Tower was always bustling with royal activity.
nodes.response: Royal residents were seldom present. Most of the time, the White Tower was managed by the keeper and housed a garrison of soldiers.

nodes.misconception: The resolution of a story will leave no unanswered questions and all conflicts resolved.
nodes.response: Sometimes there can still be a few things left open or unresolved. This can make the story more interesting and leave readers thinking about what might happen next.

nodes.misconception: Anyone can escape poverty if they just work hard enough.
nodes.response: Hard work is important, but structural barriers like low wages, lack of education, and discrimination make social mobility difficult. Support systems and fair opportunities are needed to help people escape poverty.

nodes.misconception: Jesus ascended immediately after his resurrection.
nodes.response: Jesus ascended into heaven 40 days after his resurrection according to the New Testament.

nodes.misconception: There is just one account of the resurrection.
nodes.response: The Gospel accounts all recount that Jesus was raised from the dead and appeared to his disciples in slightly different versions.

nodes.misconception: Resistance to William’s rule of England, came only from the English.
nodes.response: In 1075, two Norman earls revolted against William, and English forces helped to stop the rebellion.

nodes.misconception: The rhythm section 'plays the rhythm'. Rhythm sections are a fixed group of instruments.
nodes.response: Highlight the roles of the band and how they 'support' the singer and don't just provide rhythm for the song. There is some flexibility in the rhythm section. Not all the instruments have to be present in the music all of the time.

nodes.misconception: Winning the right to vote in 1919 led to a radical transformation in the status and position of women in society in the 1920s and 1930s.
nodes.response: Although the Representation of the People Act of 1919 was a significant turning point, Britain in the 1920s and 1930s remained a very patriarchal society.

nodes.misconception: The Voting Rights Act (1965) marked the end of protests to fight against racial injustice.
nodes.response: Many people felt the acts were too little too late as unemployment rates remained high and daily discrimination continued - for many, in the form of poverty.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that Athelstan controlled Scotland because he defeated Constantine.
nodes.response: Although Constantine lost, Athelstan only remained king of England. He became overlord of Scotland but failed to unite England and Scotland under one kingship.

nodes.misconception: Hitler was always an unpopular dictator.
nodes.response: Hitler often attracted enthusiastic crowds to his speeches. By January 1933, the popularity of Hitler and the Nazi Party had turned into an electoral success.

nodes.misconception: King Offa was solely responsible for Mercian supremacy.
nodes.response: Although it was mostly King Offa, the supremacy of Mercia was already beginning before his reign and continued for a short while afterwards.

nodes.misconception: Napoleon only ever experienced success during this period, and was never defeated.
nodes.response: Napoleon faced military setbacks (particularly at sea) during this period, usually at the hands of the British.

nodes.misconception: Julius Caesar was an emperor of the Roman Empire.
nodes.response: Julius Caesar was not an emperor of the Roman Empire but a dictator of the Roman Republic.

nodes.misconception: The River Ganges is sacred because the water heals people.
nodes.response: The river is sacred to most Hindus because of its earthly manifestation of the goddess Ganga.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that the River Nile is a river found only in Egypt.
nodes.response: The River Nile does flow through Egypt, but it also flows through 10 other countries in east Africa. It is Africa's longest river.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that rivers simply stop or disappear, rather than flow into a larger water body.
nodes.response: All rivers are part of the water cycle; water in a river flows overland along its course until it reaches a larger body of water, often at the coast. For example, water from the River Taff flows into Cardiff Bay.

nodes.misconception: Rivers are fast near the source and become slower as they flow downstream.
nodes.response: Rivers are, on average, slower in the upper course. The reason for this is due to small rivers being slowed down by friction with the bed and the banks.

nodes.misconception: There is only one type of rock, and rocks can't change.
nodes.response: Students will explore the three main types of rock found on Earth, and understand how rocks are recycled through the rock cycle.

nodes.misconception: Making an exhibition is just about hanging art.
nodes.response: Curation requires skills and knowledge. Curation can create connections and a narrative between individual works.

nodes.misconception: Puja in Buddhism is the worshipping of a god or gods, in the same way as in some other religions.
nodes.response: The Buddha is not a god, but a teacher who reached enlightenment. Puja is a way to show respect, devotion and strengthen commitment to the Buddhist path of enlightenment.

nodes.misconception: Sketchbooks have a set format, and must be presented in the 'right' way.
nodes.response: Sketchbooks are a personal record of your own creative journey, but in the GCSE course they also allow you to gain marks, so sometimes we recommend working in a certain way to help you achieve.

nodes.misconception: The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas visualised during meditation are merely imaginary or symbolic constructs rather than meaningful presences with deeper significance.
nodes.response: In Mahayana schools of Buddhism, visualising Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is seen as a method for connecting with enlightened qualities, purifying the mind, and realising one's own buddha-nature.

nodes.misconception: Swash is when a wave moves down the beach to the sea and backwash is when a wave moves up the beach from the sea.
nodes.response: The swash is the movement of the wave from the sea to the beach which brings sediment with it. Whereas the backwash is the movement of the wave from the beach to sea.

nodes.misconception: Mollie is the only character interested in sugar as a luxury.
nodes.response: Napoleon orders sugar for his table and his consumption alone. What does this tell us about the hypocrisy of the pigs?

nodes.misconception: People may have stereotypes about different places.
nodes.response: Discuss where people's stereotypes come from and emphasise the importance of using multiple sources of information to build up a more accurate picture of what a place is like.

nodes.misconception: Boulder clay is an example of sedimentary rock.
nodes.response: Boulder clay is an example of glacial till. Glacial till is an example of sedimentary deposits.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that all characters view Jamaica as an idealised homeland.
nodes.response: Explain that while Brod and Mai idealise Jamaica, Enid's more cynical view highlights the hardships she faced there, creating tension between characters' perspectives.

nodes.misconception: Jesus should have used his divine power to avoid his crucifixion.
nodes.response: Jesus went through with the crucifixion because he knew it would bring about a greater good.

nodes.misconception: Malcolm X's main philosophy was the use of violence in order to fight racial injustice.
nodes.response: Malcolm X supported Black Nationalism and encouraged black Americans to defend themselves by any means necessary, although this did endorse violence, Malcolm X spent much of his time with the Black Muslims supporting black Americans in poorer areas.

nodes.misconception: Decomposers release energy that is recycled back to plants.
nodes.response: Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste. This returns minerals to the soil which can be used by plants. It is worth stating that some decomposers are eaten by carnivores as part of food chain diagrams that include decomposers.

nodes.misconception: Peacemaking requires the use of violence to restore peace.
nodes.response: Peacemaking refers to non-violent efforts to build peace, such as reconciliation, negotiation and addressing injustice.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often overlook Simon's significance in this novel.
nodes.response: Simon is a very important character because he shows us that, in a world of evil, we can still act in a compassionate and civilised manner. Through Simon, Golding reminds us that our behaviour is a choice.

nodes.misconception: The Haitian Revolution directly inspired the abolition of slavery everywhere.
nodes.response: The events of the Haitian Revolution strengthened Britain's abolitionist movement and helped France to initially abolish slavery in 1794; but under Napoleon the threat of enslavement returned.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think the metronome matches the rhythms they play, since they previously played crotchets.
nodes.response: Pupils should play a metronome beat while the class claps quavers to highlight the metronome shows the pulse by clicking on the beats of the bar.

nodes.misconception: All instruments have a fixed role and only the drums drive the music forward.
nodes.response: The guitar and piano can be melodic as well as accompanying. Different instruments can drive the music forward, and all players in the ensemble are responsible for this.

nodes.misconception: Pupils start playing on the snare because they are used to reading left to right.
nodes.response: Emphasise that the kick is the start because it is central within the drum kit.

nodes.misconception: Pupils are familiar with the physiological changes that occur in the body when they get cold or hot, but are unaware of the role of the brain in the detection and coordination of this response.
nodes.response: The role of the hypothalamus and thermoregulatory centre in this process are clearly explained and built into the process model of managing the familiar physiological responses.

nodes.misconception: You can play an open hi-hat all the way through the bar or anywhere in the pattern.
nodes.response: The hi-hat can be played open at any point, but it shouldn't be overused, and stylistically it works well on the last quaver or off the beat.

nodes.misconception: Understanding why the physiological responses to higher or lower body temperatures occur is often confused, because although the processes themselves are familiar, the reasons behind them are not.
nodes.response: Detail has been included to explain carefully and one at a time the reasons for a range of physiological responses to high or low body temperature, and these are illustrated with clear, familiar diagrams.

nodes.misconception: The windmill is only presented as a negative.
nodes.response: Explore Snowball's initial plans. How does he view the role of the windmill? Orwell is showing how industry and progress can be exploited.

nodes.misconception: The Equal Pay Act (1970) led to women being paid the same as men.
nodes.response: Although the Equal Pay Act made it illegal to pay women less than men for doing the same work, many employers adjusted job descriptions for female workers to avoid paying them equally.

nodes.misconception: The existence of female rulers like Elizabeth I and Mary, Queen of Scots, meant that women in early modern Britain had significantly more power than in the medieval period.
nodes.response: It was extremely rare for women to wield power during this period. Early modern Britain was a patriarchal society in which society was controlled by men and the vast majority of women were excluded from all positions of power and influence.

nodes.misconception: That Jesus said that men are the 'head' of the household.
nodes.response: This is recorded in the Bible as being the words of St Paul, not Jesus.

nodes.misconception: Understanding how kidney filtration is controlled is complex, multifaceted and involves fairly obscure parts of the body so there is a lot of new content in this topic.
nodes.response: The parts of the process are broken down into individual steps, introduced with care and supporting illustrations, checked, reviewed and backed up with reinforcing tasks.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that the people of Britain formed a united kingdom at this time.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that 1st century CE Britain was made up of various Celtic people, kingdoms and tribes.

nodes.misconception: Rome was always an Empire.
nodes.response: Before the Roman Empire was founded, Rome was first ruled by kings and then Rome became a republic.

nodes.misconception: Romantic music is romantic (i.e. about love).
nodes.response: Romantic music is generally expressive and emotional, but is not necessarily linked to the emotion of love. The emotions can be anything from dramatic and terrifying to dark and mournful. The name comes from a broader artistic movement.

nodes.misconception: Romantic music is related to love and romance.
nodes.response: This is not the case - the name is not related to that. Romantic composers focused on creating expression, emotion and evocative moods in their music. Sometimes this would have links with love, but not always.

nodes.misconception: That there was one hieroglyph (picture) equivalent to each letter of the English alphabet.
nodes.response: The Ancient Egyptians did not have an alphabet in the same way we do today. Hieroglyphs represented sounds and sometimes whole words. There were a lot more hieroglyphs than there are letters of the alphabet.

nodes.misconception: The belief that Margaret of Anjou was a vicious and unpleasant woman.
