nodes.response: A woman who held power would have likely been criticised in the medieval period and Yorkists would also have wanted to show her in an unfavourable light.

nodes.misconception: Sitting volleyball is only for people with disabilities.
nodes.response: Sitting volleyball is a Paralympic sport, however it is an inclusive and adapted sport that anyone can play regardless of ability. Players have to move quickly around the court using their upper bodies frequently in a seated position.

nodes.misconception: When identifying spellings for 's', 'ce' and 'c' can be mixed up.
nodes.response: Use sound buttoning to help, especially when looking at words with split digraphs.

nodes.misconception: Children may think 'ce' represents the 's' sound in 'ice' and 'face'.
nodes.response: Use sound buttoning as a strategy when you know it will reinforce the spelling pattern (it doesn't always work).

nodes.misconception: All Christians celebrate the sacraments.
nodes.response: Many Christians do celebrate the sacraments, but not all Christians. For example, Quakers do not celebrate the sacraments.

nodes.misconception: It is perfectly possible for pupils to be highly numerate but struggle with the spatial awareness needed to visualise / imagine whether a 2D net will fold together to form a 2D shape.
nodes.response: As part of the lesson design process you may wish to incorporate manipulatives such as construction materials for those pupils whose learning needs scaffolding. As with all scaffolding, aim to move pupils away from this when you can.

nodes.misconception: All Christians see the sanctity of life as a moral absolute.
nodes.response: Different denominations and individuals may have varying perspectives on whether extrinsic factors such as dignity or well-being impinge on the sanctity of life.

nodes.misconception: 'Equal chance' means the same as 'even chance'.
nodes.response: When a trial has more than two possible outcomes which are all equally likely to happen, each outcome has less than an even chance of happening. E.g. each number on a dice has the same likelihood of being rolled, but each is less than an even chance.

nodes.misconception: Britain and competing European powers met at the Berlin Conference before the scramble for Africa had begun.
nodes.response: Britain and competing European powers had already been 'scrambling' for Africa for the majority of the 19th century. The Berlin Conference was an attempt to put an end to the fighting between European powers over Africa's land and resources.

nodes.misconception: Children will often remember one of the loops for the f but forget the other.
nodes.response: Lots of modelling and emphasising that the letter f needs to 'hold hands' with the letter in front and behind it.

nodes.misconception: Children will often want to take their pencil off to form the join.
nodes.response: Emphasise the flowing motion of cursive writing. The letters need to be joined together so the pencil needs to stay on the page.

nodes.misconception: Children will often remember one of the loops for the f but forget the other.
nodes.response: Lots of modelling and emphasising that the letter f needs to 'hold hands' with the letter in front and behind it.

nodes.misconception: The order of the Seder doesn’t matter. You can do it any way you want.
nodes.response: The word “Seder” means “order,” and the Seder follows a special, set sequence. Each step and food is part of this order to help tell the story clearly and meaningfully.

nodes.misconception: Special places or landscapes all look the same.
nodes.response: Special landscapes can look and feel very different to each other. They are special because they make you feel different things like awe and wonder.

nodes.misconception: The Shahadah is simply a phrase and not a belief.
nodes.response: The Shahadah is more than just words, it involves committing your life to live as a Muslim.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that objects in space are flat, circular shapes rather than spherical
nodes.response: Provide plenty of opportunities for children to use 3D models to represent the Earth, Sun and Moon, and look at images and simulations

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that objects in space are flat, circular shapes rather than spherical.
nodes.response: Provide plenty of opportunities for children to use 3D models to represent the Earth, Sun and Moon, and look at images and simulations.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often mix up what changes happen in response to exercise and what changes happen as a long term adaptation to training.
nodes.response: Short-term responses of the body are what happens as soon as we start exercising to cope with it, but if we train regularly, then the body adapts to be better able to cope with the stress of exercise and hence work more efficiently in performance.

nodes.misconception: Pupils spell the ending of professions 'cion'.
nodes.response: Focus on the difference between -ion and -ian endings.  Say the word how it's spelt to reinforce this: mu -si -ci -an.

nodes.misconception: The curriculum words 'reigh', 'island' and 'February' can be mis-spelt, without the silent letters.
nodes.response: Practise saying the word how it is spelt, e.g. Feb-ru-ar-y.  Use the 'naughty letters' strategy to emphasise unusual letters in the words.

nodes.misconception: Pupils miss out letters in 'century' because they cannot hear all the sounds.
nodes.response: Say the word slowly, as it is spelt, in order to empahsise all the letters: cen -tur -y.

nodes.misconception: Wildfires are all ignited naturally.
nodes.response: Wildfires can be ignited by natural (e.g. lightning) or human causes (e.g. campfires).

nodes.misconception: People think the survey and Domesday Book are one and the same thing.
nodes.response: In fact, the survey was ordered in 1085, and later compiled into what became known as Domesday Book.

nodes.misconception: The Sikh diaspora are all immigrants from the Punjab region, now in India and Pakistan.
nodes.response: The Sikh diaspora includes many people from countries in East Africa e.g. Uganda.

nodes.misconception: When annotating, you should highlight, underline and circle interesting things. You don't need to write anything down as you will remember what you thought.
nodes.response: Symbols, highlights and underlinings are all useful, but only if accompanied by short written notes which remind you what it was you found interesting. Otherwise your symbols become meaningless.

nodes.misconception: Only silk was traded along the Silk Road.
nodes.response: Silk was a primary commodity for a long time along the Silk Road, but there were many different goods and ideas that were traded between East and West along the trade route.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may be uncertain about which angle pairs with which side.
nodes.response: The angle is paired with the side length that is opposite.

nodes.misconception: Students may think that the White Tower was the only castle in Norman London.
nodes.response: In fact, there were two other castles in Norman London: Baynard's Castle and Montfichet's Tower.

nodes.misconception: The six articles of faith are only believed by Sunni Muslims.
nodes.response: Most Muslims (both Sunni and Shia) hold beliefs about tawhid, prophecy, holy books, angels, the Day of Judgement and God's power, but they may not ascribe to them as the 'six articles of faith'.

nodes.misconception: The six key beliefs are only believed by Sunni Muslims.
nodes.response: Most Muslims (both Sunni and Shia) hold beliefs about tawhid, prophecy, holy books, angels, the Day of Judgement and God's power, but they may not ascribe to them as the 'six articles of faith'.

nodes.misconception: Generosity and morality are qualities solely focused on external actions or rituals.
nodes.response: It is also about cultivating a selfless mindset. True generosity transcends material things and is rooted in an attitude of openness and kindness. Morality is about acting in a way which includes mental discipline and mindfulness.

nodes.misconception: Wisdom means gaining intellectual knowledge or philosophical understanding.
nodes.response: In the context of the perfections, wisdom isn’t about collecting facts or debating philosophy, it is about experiencing the truth of emptiness (sunyata).

nodes.misconception: Patience is often misunderstood as merely passively tolerating suffering or discomfort.
nodes.response: Patience is an active quality of acceptance, equanimity, and understanding. It involves the ability to face difficulties without anger, frustration, or attachment, whilst maintaining a sense of compassion and wisdom.

nodes.misconception: Pupils commonly convert units incorrectly, multiplying when they should divide or dividing when they should multiply.
nodes.response: It can help to relate the unit conversions in the lesson to an everyday example, e.g. pounds to pence.

nodes.misconception: Pupils commonly convert units incorrectly, multiplying when they should divide or dividing when they should multiply.
nodes.response: It can help to relate the unit conversions in the lesson to an everyday example, e.g. pounds to pence.

nodes.misconception: Figurative language, like metaphors, is not used in presentations.
nodes.response: Stress how much stronger presentations can be when it allows the audience to make associations with objects and items they are familiar with.

nodes.misconception: Gravity only acts close to the surface of a planet.
nodes.response: Provide examples of motions caused by gravitational forces acting over huge distances of space, such as the orbits of planets.

nodes.misconception: Annotating means highlighting everything you think is important in a text.
nodes.response: Annotating is a skill that requires time and thought. Using symbols and short notes makes your annotations helpful and understandable, even if you come back to them at a much later date.

nodes.misconception: All Christians view the song of Deborah as a supporting text for female leadership in religion.
nodes.response: There are different views on the leadership of women in religion; two examples are complementarian and egalitarian. These views will impact therefore how someone may view the song of Deborah in relation to supporting female leadership in religion.

nodes.misconception: Music technology consists solely of DAWs and computer-based technology.
nodes.response: For modern musicians, computer-based tools such as DAWs are a brilliant way of using technology. However, music technology is much broader than this - synthesisers, amplification, turntables and drum machines are just a few examples.

nodes.misconception: Antarctica is a country.
nodes.response: Antarctica is a continent.

nodes.misconception: Poorer people in Afghanistan supported the communist PDPA government.
nodes.response: The PDPA's land reforms were tainted by corruption and angered many poorer Afghans because they received poor quality land. Many Afghans opposed the PDPA's attempts to create a secular society, which they saw as an attack on their faith and culture.

nodes.misconception: All communist countries were members of the Warsaw Pact.
nodes.response: The Warsaw Pact was primarily a European military alliance so non-European communist countries like China and Cuba were not members. Some European countries like Yugoslavia were never members while others joined and then left like Albania in 1968.

nodes.misconception: The USA was in the lead throughout the Space Race.
nodes.response: The USSR beat the USA to launch the first satellite into orbit and to put both the first man and first woman in space.

nodes.misconception: The different 'kinds' of EM radiation are different phenomena to each other and to visible light. Pupils may also think all radiation is dangerous, none is natural and that light is not radiation.
nodes.response: Each 'kind' of EM radiation is the same phenomena as light (i.e. waves/ripples in electric and magnetic fields) just with different frequencies and wavelengths. Try to refer to different frequencies/frequency ranges rather than different 'kinds'.

nodes.misconception: The different 'kinds' of EM radiation are different phenomena to each other and to visible light. Pupils may also think all radiation is dangerous, none is natural and that light is not radiation.
nodes.response: Each 'kind' of EM radiation is the same phenomena as light (i.e. waves/ripples in electric and magnetic fields) just with different frequencies and wavelengths. Try to refer to different frequencies/frequency ranges rather than different 'kinds'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils can find it challenging to see how the movements of Earth as seen from the perspective of space (looking back at Earth) give rise to the observations experienced from Earth's surface.
nodes.response: Model the motions of objects in space with pupils as part of the model (i.e. representing Earth, moving as Earth moves) and with pupils observing the model. This enables them to experience how the same motion appears from both perspectives.

nodes.misconception: Revolutionary ideas failed to spread from France to other European countries.
nodes.response: Revolutionary ideas did spread to other European countries, but they did not cause any successful revolutions.

nodes.misconception: Hobbes believed freedom is bad.
nodes.response: Hobbes did not oppose all freedom, but argued that unlimited freedom in the state of nature leads to chaos.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may reach false conclusions by not following the Statistical Enquiry Cycle and skipping stages.
nodes.response: Ask pupils to consider trying to draw conclusions from a large data set of raw values, where no processing or representation has taken place, to highlight the need for that stage in particular.

nodes.misconception: That the Statute of Labourers immediately forced all peasants to return to their home manors and to cease negotiating higher wages.
nodes.response: Through the interpretations section of the lesson, draw out the point that the Statute of Labourers was unenforceable in many cases.

nodes.misconception: Temperate grasslands are the only places in the world where cereal crops are grown.
nodes.response: Whilst temperate grasslands are significant providers of much of the world’s wheat and other cereal crops and referred to as 'breadbaskets', they are not the only places in the world where these crops are grown.

nodes.misconception: A storm hydrograph shows rainfall.
nodes.response: A storm hydrograph shows river discharge changes over time, not just rainfall.

nodes.misconception: A promise is easy to make and keep.
nodes.response: Promises are often long term and are difficult to keep.

nodes.misconception: The wise men and shepherds all visited Jesus at the same time.
nodes.response: The wise men visited at a later time after the birth of Jesus.

nodes.misconception: Christians might be angry at the destruction of a cathedral and seek revenge.
nodes.response: The people of Coventry rebuilt their cathedral as a symbol of hope in a better world based on forgiveness and reconciliation.

nodes.misconception: Antisemitism is a modern experience.
nodes.response: This story shows that antisemitism goes back at least 3,000 years.

nodes.misconception: A menorah is just a decorative candle-holder.
nodes.response: A menorah has a deep significance for Jews as a symbol of G_d and the days of creation.

nodes.misconception: Festivals remember happy occasions.
nodes.response: Some remember good overcoming evil.

nodes.misconception: The Bible says that things always go well when you believe in God.
nodes.response: Joseph, and many other Bible characters, faced great difficulties even though they had faith.

nodes.misconception: Prayer is more important than caring for others.
nodes.response: Caring is as important as prayer.

nodes.misconception: Ravana is just evil and bad without any reason.
nodes.response: Ravana is not simply evil. He is a powerful king with many good qualities but is also prideful and arrogant. His flaws lead him to make poor choices, like kidnapping Sita, which makes him a complex character.

nodes.misconception: Russia and the USSR are the same.
nodes.response: Russia was the largest part of the USSR, but they are not the same. The USSR was a union of 15 republics, including Russia. It dissolved in 1991, and each republic, like Ukraine and Georgia, became independent.

nodes.misconception: One of the blind men was correct and the others were wrong about the elephant.
nodes.response: All the blind men touched a different part of the elephant and so did not fully understand what an elephant was like.

nodes.misconception: The Khalsa was created only for warriors who fight in battles.
nodes.response: The Khalsa was created for all Sikhs who live by a set of values, such as honesty, bravery, kindness, and service to others.

nodes.misconception: A neighbour is the person who lives next door to you.
nodes.response: Anyone outside of your family is a neighbour.

nodes.misconception: Jesus only taught stories to his followers that were simple to understand.
nodes.response: Sometimes Jesus told stories that contained a challenging message for the audience.

nodes.misconception: Hindu deities are often depicted in strange colours.
nodes.response: Images of Hindu deities are highly symbolic and colour often connects to deeper meanings about the deity.

nodes.misconception: Some problems are so big that you can't do anything about them.
nodes.response: Everyone can do at least one thing to make a difference.

nodes.misconception: Namaste is simply a way of saying ‘hello’ for Hindus.
nodes.response: Namaste symbolises a deep respect and belief that all humans contain a spark of the divine.

nodes.misconception: All Hindu stories come from the same source.
nodes.response: There are many sources for Hindu stories. Each story helps Hindus understand more about God and the world.

nodes.misconception: All streets outside schools across the country have all of these features and look the same.
nodes.response: The street outside your school is unique to your school. There might be all, some or none of these features. There could be features outside your school that are not mentioned here.

nodes.misconception: The string instruments can only be identified by pitch. The woodwind instruments are made of wood.
nodes.response: The pitch of the instruments does overlap slightly, so it's important to emphasise that the timbre of each instrument is slightly different. Most woodwind instruments were originally made of wood but the flute and the saxophone are now made of metal.

nodes.misconception: What constitutes a reflex response, and how they are generated in the body is often confused and muddled, leading to an incorrect mix between a standard neural pathway and the reflex pathway.
nodes.response: The reflex pathway is clearly stated and explained, and it is compared to the standard neural pathway. Plenty of examples of reflexes are given, including those that occur in other organisms, and there is a quick practical to try too.

nodes.misconception: Students often rush the ending of their work - particularly if they are writing in timed conditions.
nodes.response: The ending is arguably the most important part of the piece of writing. Students need to leave their reader with a clear message that is memorable. The ending ties together the threads of the argument and reinforces the writer's viewpoint.

nodes.misconception: Students may think that each strand of DNA is the same without recognising one strand is inverted.
nodes.response: The slides specifically mention the second strand is inverted and this is also reinforced using diagrams of inverted nucleotides wherever possible.

nodes.misconception: DNA is living and not necessarily a chemical.
nodes.response: Discussing that DNA is a chemical molecule and showing how it is made up of smaller chemical groups, and then modelling this chemical structure.

nodes.misconception: Jakarta’s suburbs are poor and unplanned with informal settlements.
nodes.response: Jakarta’s suburbs include both wealthy and mid-income areas, many of which are well-planned and developed (e.g. Pondok Indah, Kelapa Gading).

nodes.misconception: The inner core is hotter than the outer core so the inner core must be liquid (molten rock) while the outer core is solid rock.
nodes.response: In fact, although the inner core is hotter than the outer core, the inner core is solid while the outer core is molten and liquid. This is because the pressure is so great in the inner core that it prevents the rock from melting.

nodes.misconception: Which side of the heart is the left when you look at the body and which side is oxygenated versus deoxygenated.
nodes.response: The left side of the heart is nearest your left armpit and carries oxygenated blood, the right side of the heart has deoxygenated blood (remember: LORD - left, oxygenated and right, deogygenated).

nodes.misconception: The triangular trade was a simple trading route with three main points.
nodes.response: The triangular trade was a complex system of trade, that is often simplified to help us better understand it.

nodes.misconception: The Norman conquest was fully achieved by the victory at the Battle of Hastings.
nodes.response: In reality, there were many defiant Anglo-Saxons ready to carry on fighting and it took time for William to gain meaningful control over a hostile Anglo-Saxon population.

nodes.misconception: The Norman conquest was fully achieved by the victory at the Battle of Hastings.
nodes.response: In reality, there were many defiant Anglo-Saxons ready to carry on fighting and it took time for William to gain meaningful control over a hostile Anglo-Saxon population.

nodes.misconception: Quilts are just blankets or decorative items and don’t have any deeper meaning.
nodes.response: While quilts are often used for warmth or decoration, many artists use quilts to share powerful stories and messages. Quilts can be a way for artists to speak out about important issues and make sure voices are heard.

nodes.misconception: Successful empires dominate and subjugate the conquered people within the empire in order to keep them loyal.
nodes.response: The Mali aristocracy adopted a successful 'hands off' approach to governance, allowing the different kingdoms within the empire a great degree of autonomy.

nodes.misconception: Children may think the root word will help determine the spelling, but this does not always help.
nodes.response: Review links to root words when helpful, but encourage use of the rule about vowels and consonants to determine the spelling.

nodes.misconception: Suffragists were the same as suffragettes.
nodes.response: One way for pupils to remember the difference is that the suffraGETtes wanted to GET things done - deeds not words.

nodes.misconception: When calculating the resultant vector, pupils can incorrectly sum vectors due to opposite directions or proportions of vectors.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to write a clear vector pathway; sometimes using highlighters can help visualize this pathway.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle with mathematical proof, especially using other knowledge within it.
nodes.response: Explain to pupils that there are many different styles of mathematical proof but all are showing that a particular fact holds true for all.

nodes.misconception: We cannot use electricity from solar cells when it is cloudy or at night.
nodes.response: Explanation of how energy can be stored in batteries to be used when it is needed.

nodes.misconception: When finding the surface area of the cone, pupils may find the curved surface area but forget to include circular base of the cone.
nodes.response: By re-reading the question, and inspecting any given diagram, pupils can check if the cone is open or closed and therefore if they need to include the circular base in their calculation.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that a cone is a pyramid.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that a pyramid has a polygonal base, so a cone cannot be a pyramid as the base is a circle, which is not a polygon.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may forget the constant '4' when calculating the surface area.
nodes.response: Show the demonstration of the formula of the surface area using a different spherical fruit to see that it is always 4 regardless of the size of the sphere. You can also relate it to the 1/2 in the formula of the area of triangle.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that the ‘fittest’, as in ‘survival of the fittest’, means the most physically fit or healthy, rather than the most suited to the environment and conditions.
nodes.response: Using the examples in the slide deck, clearly explain that when we refer to the ‘fittest’ living things surviving, we mean those that are best suited to the conditions they are living in.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may assume that tangents can be drawn in slightly different directions at the same point on a circle.
nodes.response: The tangent at a point on a circle can only be drawn in one possible direction. The tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at that point.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that all circle theorems are about angles.
nodes.response: Circle theorems can be about angles or lengths in diagrams containing a circle.

nodes.misconception: Students may think protocols like HTTP or FTP operate at all layers, or that TCP and IP are the only protocols in the model.
nodes.response: Specific protocols perform unique functions at dedicated TCP/IP layers.

nodes.misconception: Rainforests must have the most nutritious soil as they have such a lot of plants and such tall trees.
nodes.response: Temperate deciduous forests have more nutrient rich soil than other forests as trees lose their leaves, meaning there is a lot of leaf litter and the climate is not too cold for decomposers.

nodes.misconception: Moses made up the Ten Commandments himself.
nodes.response: Jewish people believe that God gave these special rules to Moses on a mountain.

nodes.misconception: Wars are only won on the battlefield.
nodes.response: A variety of factors influence the outcome of a war, such as a nation's economy, geography, and popular sentiment towards the war.

nodes.misconception: Children may not understand what they are able to do to protect the environment and animal habitats.
nodes.response: Explain to the children the different ways in which humans can make positive choices to combat climate change.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to understand other's perspectives (i.e. where others feel they belong).
nodes.response: Remind pupils that one person's feeling of belonging may be different to someone else's and the importance of perspective.

nodes.misconception: Children may find it difficult to understand some of the themes and the connections between them.
nodes.response: Allow time to discuss the connections between the three themes at the end of cycle 1. E.g. Collaboration can be a form of resourcefulness.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may be unfamiliar with terms such as setting and plot.
nodes.response: Spend time contextualising the terms using stories they will know well, such as the deep, dark woods as the setting for 'The Gruffalo'.

nodes.misconception: That Snowball isn't deceptive.
nodes.response: Does Snowball enjoy the "milk and apples" too? What is he awarded after the Battle of the Cowshed and how does this position Snowball?

nodes.misconception: Children might think that all families look like their own.
nodes.response: Emphasise the idea that all families are different and families go beyond just the people you live with.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to distinguish between what makes them happy and what they do to stay happy.
nodes.response: Use examples from your own experiences. Discuss that our feelings may change, but there are strategies you use to keep a positive mood going. Emphasise all of the things that the characters do to help to keep their happiness going.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may not be aware of their own nationality or background.
nodes.response: Prepare this knowledge about pupils' backgrounds in advance. Use a globe or map to pinpoint and discuss different places around the world. Ensure you give children autonomy to discuss what they see as their culture regardless of place of birth.

nodes.misconception: That Orwell presents "good" leaders and "bad" leaders.
nodes.response: Think about the impact of Mr. Jones and the pigs on the animals' lives. Is it easy to distinguish which one is better or worse?

nodes.misconception: Children may have questions around the role they can play in protecting the world. They may not understand the link between actions they can take and the positive effects of it globally.
nodes.response: Discuss some examples of simple actions we can take and how far reaching the impact can be even if we can't see it. E.g. Reducing our use of energy will combat global warming which will protect sea ice for polar bears.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may be uncertain of what some of the scientific vocabulary means, making the story difficult to follow.
nodes.response: As you are reading, gloss over key vocabulary, such as "research" and "hypothesis" by providing a definition linked to the events in the story using the illustrations.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to write their own sentence about what they are responsible for.
nodes.response: If necessary, pupils could just draw a picture and have the sentence scribed for them as the primary focus for this session is engaging with the text and understanding what responsibility means.

nodes.misconception: The dip down for the third join can be challenging at first, especially when joining to the letter e.
nodes.response: Model with emphasis the dip down so that children can see its importance and purpose. Give them time to really look at the join to the letter e. Allow them to realise themselves that the dip down begins the formation of the letter e.

nodes.misconception: Children can struggle to get the gap size between the letters correct with this join.
nodes.response: Model this join lots emphasising 'we dip down and across and then form the next letter so they can still hold hands. We don't want them to be far away from each other'.

nodes.misconception: Children can struggle to get the gap size between the letters correct with this join.
nodes.response: Model this join lots emphasising 'we dip down and across and then form the next letter so they can still hold hands, we don't want them to be far away from each other'.

nodes.misconception: Children can struggle to get the gap size between the letters correct with this join.
nodes.response: Model this join lots emphasising 'we dip down and across and then form the next letter so they can still hold hands, we don't want them to be far away from each other'.

nodes.misconception: Children can struggle to get the gap size between the letters correct with this join.
nodes.response: Model this join lots emphasising 'we dip down and across and then form the next letter so they can still hold hands, we don't want them to be far away from each other'.

nodes.misconception: Children can struggle to get the gap size between the letters correct with this join.
nodes.response: Model this join lots emphasising 'we dip down and across and then form the next letter so they can still hold hands, we don't want them to be far away from each other'.

nodes.misconception: The jewels refer to riches or physical treasure.
nodes.response: The jewels are highly valued principles and institutions.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that the kingdoms are places in Egypt.
nodes.response: Kingdoms are are periods of time in Egyptian history; the Old Kingdom, the Middle Kingdom and the New Kingdom.

nodes.misconception: Tinkercad is a paid-for software that will cost schools money and is unsafe to use.
nodes.response: Tinkercad is free to use and schools can set up their own classrooms for pupils to work safely in.

nodes.misconception: Britain was always involved in the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
nodes.response: Britain became involved in the trade in the 1500s, initially selling enslaved people onto plantations in Spanish and Portuguese colonies.

nodes.misconception: That calling someone a 'monster' means that you find them terrifying.
nodes.response: While calling someone a 'monster' can mean you find them terrifying, it can also be a way of ridiculing someone and showing your dislike.

nodes.misconception: Corporal punishment is banned everywhere.
nodes.response: It is still legal in over 100 countries in the home, in some schools (including 17 US states), and as a criminal sentence in around 30–35 countries.

nodes.misconception: Prison always helps people change for the better.
nodes.response: Without proper support, prisoners may be more likely to reoffend after release due to negative influences, lack of rehabilitation and poor mental health care.

nodes.misconception: The persons of the Trinity are three separate gods.
nodes.response: Christians believe in only one God, who is represented in three distrinct persons.

nodes.misconception: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three separate gods.
nodes.response: Most Christians believe in the Oneness of God and that all three Persons of the Trinity are present in only one God, therefore the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three separate gods.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that Troy was a real place and that the Trojan War was a real conflict.
nodes.response: The story of the Trojan War is from Greek mythology. Myths are stories that people have told by word of mouth for thousands of years, some people do claim that myths are true but they are in fact fictional stories - they did not happen in real life.

nodes.misconception: Topical rainforests are cold and wet.
nodes.response: In tropical rainforests it is hot, this heat actually causes the rain by creating a lot of evaporation and rising air, which then cools and condenses to form clouds which rain.

nodes.misconception: That the Congo rainforest is only found in the DRC.
nodes.response: The Congo rainforest is found in the Congo Basin, which spans six countries in Africa: Cameroon, Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

nodes.misconception: The USA always considered it had a responsibility to protect Europe from threats.
nodes.response: Before the Second World War, the USA had a policy of isolationism which meant not getting involved in the affairs of other countries.

nodes.misconception: The USA always considered it had a responsibility to protect Europe from threats.
nodes.response: Before the Second World War, the USA had a policy of isolationism which meant not getting involved in the affairs of other countries.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that the draugr is simply a physical monster with no deeper significance or symbolism.
nodes.response: While the draugr is indeed a fearsome physical entity, it also symbolises deeper themes such as death, decay and the persistence of fear. In Norse mythology, draugrs are more than just monsters; they embody the fears and anxieties of the living.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might believe that writing a summary means including all details from the story.
nodes.response: Explain that a summary should only include the most important events and main ideas in a concise manner. Remind them that the goal is to capture the essence of the story, not every detail.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that a headline alone is enough to convey the entire story of an article.
nodes.response: Explain that while a headline grabs attention and hints at the article's content, it's the subheading and body text that provide the full details and context. Emphasise the importance of each element working together to inform the reader.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may believe that the conclusion should introduce new ideas or quotes.
nodes.response: Explain that a conclusion should summarise the main points and restate the thesis in a new way, rather than introducing new evidence or arguments. Its purpose is to reinforce what has already been discussed, reinforcing the main arguments.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might believe that tension in a story is only created through dramatic events or actions.
nodes.response: Tension can also be built through subtle elements like descriptive language, sensory details and the anticipation of what might happen next.

nodes.misconception: A thesis statement only needs to focus on one part of the book.
nodes.response: A thesis statement should address the overarching argument of your essay, which means it needs to consider the entire text.

nodes.misconception: A script is just dialogue between characters and doesn't need any other elements
nodes.response: While dialogue is a crucial part of a script, it's not the only component. A script also includes stage directions, which provide important instructions on how actors should move, behave, and speak.

nodes.misconception: Students might think that making an inference is the same as guessing randomly without any evidence.
nodes.response: Inferences are not random guesses. They are logical conclusions drawn from clues or evidence presented in the text or context.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think all draugr are depicted in Norse mythology and in 'The Twisted Tree' in the same way.
nodes.response: While draugr in Norse mythology generally share traits their specific appearances can vary between stories. Rachel Burge's portrayal in 'The Twisted Tree' offers her unique interpretation, reflecting the novel's narrative and atmosphere.

nodes.misconception: Newspaper articles must strictly adhere to factual reporting without any creative elements.
nodes.response: While newspaper articles are based on factual reporting, they often incorporate language devices like puns, alliteration and sensationalist language in headlines and sometimes throughout the article. These elements are used to engage readers.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that inferences are just guesses without any evidence.
nodes.response: Inferences are not guesses; they are conclusions drawn from evidence in the text. For example, Burge describes the fog as "snaking" around Martha. We infer that it is dangerous and sinister because the word "snake" often implies danger and malice.

nodes.misconception: Stage directions are just suggestions and don't need to be followed exactly.
nodes.response: Stage directions are essential parts of the script that provide important guidance on how the scene should be performed. They help create the atmosphere, convey emotions and ensure the story is told as the writer intended.

nodes.misconception: All quotations need to be analysed in depth.
nodes.response: Not all quotations need the same level of analysis. Main quotations are central to your argument and should be analysed to show how they support your thesis. Supporting quotations are used to reinforce the point made with the main quotations.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think symbols in the novel have only one clear meaning.
nodes.response: Explain that symbols often have multiple meanings. For example, Martha's blindness can represent family secrets, vulnerability and hidden truths. Encourage looking for different interpretations.

nodes.misconception: Gothic literature is only about horror and scary elements.
nodes.response: While Gothic literature often includes elements of horror, such as supernatural occurrences and eerie settings, it also explores complex themes like human psychology, societal anxieties and the supernatural as a metaphor for deeper fears or desires.

nodes.misconception: Students might think that all stories fit perfectly into a traditional narrative arc with only one climax.
nodes.response: While many stories follow a traditional narrative arc, some can have multiple climaxes or may not fit perfectly into the structure. The narrative arc is a helpful guide, but it's important to recognise that stories can vary and still be effective.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might confuse compound and complex sentences, thinking that any sentence with more than one clause is a complex sentence.
nodes.response: A compound sentence has two main clauses that can each stand alone as separate sentences, joined by a coordinating conjunction. In contrast, a complex sentence has one main clause and at least one subordinate clause that cannot stand alone.

nodes.misconception: Pupils might think that the use of a formal tone and third person point of view is only necessary for professional journalism and not applicable to other forms of writing.
nodes.response: Explain that while formal tone and third person are essential in professional journalism, they are also important in many other types of writing, including more localised articles like this.

nodes.misconception: The USSR immediately refused to cooperate with the USA after a U2 was show down in May 1960.
nodes.response: The USSR still attended the Paris Summit but walked out when the US refused to apologise for spying on it.

nodes.misconception: The Republic of Ireland is part of the United Kingdom.
nodes.response: The Republic of Ireland is part of Europe.

nodes.misconception: Migration tends to be for negative reasons.
nodes.response: Although the news may focus on migration due to conflict or other negative reasons, people also choose to move for positive reasons.

nodes.misconception: The UK’s climate is the same across the country.
nodes.response: Students will understand that the UK’s climate varies between different regions due to latitude, altitude and air masses.

nodes.misconception: That all coastlines are sandy beaches.
nodes.response: Not all coastlines are sandy beaches. Some coastlines have beaches of stones called shingle, and some coastlines only have cliffs without any beach.

nodes.misconception: Most of our imports in the UK come from China.
nodes.response: Most of our imports in the UK come from the US and EU countries.

nodes.misconception: Pupils assume that Slieve Donard is the smallest mountain in the UK.
nodes.response: Ensure that pupils know that Slieve Donard is not the smallest mountain in the UK, but it is the smallest out of the highest peaks in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

nodes.misconception: Ireland is part of the UK
nodes.response: Northern Ireland is part of the UK.

nodes.misconception: When reading the values of the trigonometric functions during the explanation slides and the tasks, pupils may think that all the values taken from the graphs are fully accurate.
nodes.response: Explain that many of the values from the trigonometric functions have digits beyond the second decimal place. However, two decimal places is a reasonable degree of accuracy for reading values from the graphs during this lesson.

nodes.misconception: A river has the most energy in the upper course.
nodes.response: The river does not have that much energy in the upper course as there is not a lot of water in the river.

nodes.misconception: Harold Godwinson would help his brother Tostig.
nodes.response: Harold’s ambitions to be king meant he did little to help his brother Tostig. If Harold became king, he would want to avoid making enemies of Mercia and Northumbria. He wanted to show the Witan that he was loyal to England, beyond his family.

nodes.misconception: Global citizenship is not just about helping others in distant communities.
nodes.response: It involves recognising our interconnectedness with people and the planet, meaning that the actions we take in our everyday lives have a far-reaching impact. Global citizens take personal responsibility for their own environmental practices.

nodes.misconception: Students can think a motif is a symbol used once or think it is deployed in the same way as a semantic field.
nodes.response: Remind them of the etymology - there has to be movement and change of the motif.  A semantic field does not have to be symbolic.

nodes.misconception: Children may not think it possible to replace a vital organ such as the heart with one from another person, let alone an animal bred specifically for this purpose!
nodes.response: It is important to portray a balanced argument for children to consider and debate, and for them to appreciate that no-one specifically is right or wrong.

nodes.misconception: Christians within the same tradition or denomination have the same views on using animals for food.
nodes.response: In reality, even within the same denomination, Christians can have different views based on personal beliefs, scripture interpretations and culture. Some follow official teachings, while others make their own ethical choices.

nodes.misconception: Rock is a specific, narrow genre in itself.
nodes.response: Rock is a very broad term for lots of different musical genres, spanning a wide range of influences and using very different musical features. There are many sub-genres of rock, including grunge, punk rock and heavy metal.

nodes.misconception: Dominion is the opposite of stewardship.
nodes.response: Dominion is seen as authority or power, but, in common with stewardship, it is usually seen as including a duty to be responsible.

nodes.misconception: There is often confusion between guerilla and gorilla!
nodes.response: Same sound, different spelling, very different meaning!  'Guerilla' comes from the Spanish word 'guerra', meaning 'war'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may have the impression that all Vikings were fierce, scary warriors.
nodes.response: Some Vikings were warriors, but not all. Vikings were also traders, farmers and settlers.

nodes.misconception: Sunlight is yellow(ish), not white.
nodes.response: Show pupils a yellow light (and illuminate white paper beneath a yellow light) and compare it to sunlight to show that sunlight is white.

nodes.misconception: Oratorios and anthems are essentially the same - they are both religious, with similar musical features.
nodes.response: Anthems often are a capella, whereas oratorios always have orchestral accompaniment. Oratorios are long pieces of music, consisting of numerous songs that tell a biblical story. Anthems are shorter songs that are used as part of a Christian service.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may confuse the slant height (which is needed to find the curved surface area of the cone) with the perpendicular height (which is needed to find the volume of the cone).
nodes.response: Remind pupils that for any volume calculation, three perpendicular lengths are multiplied and the slant height is not perpendicular to the base in a right cone. They may need to use Pythagoras' theorem to find the perpendicular height.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may use the edge length as the perpendicular height when calculating the volume.
nodes.response: Remind pupils that for any volume calculation, three perpendicular lengths are multiplied and in most pyramids the edge of a triangle is not perpendicular to the base. Also the edge of the triangles can be different in the pyramid.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may multiply the radius of the sphere by the constant before cubing it.
nodes.response: Remind pupils of the order of operations and the need to cube the radius before multiplying by the constants in the formula.

nodes.misconception: Vowels sound the same in Spanish and English.
nodes.response: Although the letters look the same, the vowel sounds are different in Spanish and English.

nodes.misconception: Vowels are pronounced the same in French and in English.
nodes.response: The vowels [a] [e] [i] are pronounced differently in French and English.

nodes.misconception: The war had very little impact on Ireland.
nodes.response: Irish calls for independence were delayed by the outbreak of war, and then further delayed in 1918.

nodes.misconception: The Americans won the War of Independence because they had a better army.
nodes.response: For much of the war, the American army was a poorly trained militia. Whilst they fought bravely and Washington proved to be an able general, they received significant support from France and Spain which swung the balance of the conflict.

nodes.misconception: That battles are always fought on land, by soldiers or warriors who are physically fighting each other.
nodes.response: Battles can be fought many ways - some Ancient Greek battles were land based and warriors used chariots and weapons like javelins. Other battles were at sea using boats that would be rammed into the enemy and archers that would fire arrows at them.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that new water is formed by the water cycle.
nodes.response: The amount of water on earth is the same as it always has been. It is constant. Water can be distributed and stored in different ways and in different places over time but new water is never added to or created by the water cycle.

nodes.misconception: In, v = f x λ, speed is dependent on frequency and wavelength, rather than the medium.
nodes.response: Focus on speed being property of a medium and equation not being as an equation with three interdependent variables.

nodes.misconception: That a turning point is a temporary change.
nodes.response: A turning point is usually a major, decisive and permanent change.

nodes.misconception: We can translate weather phrases word for word from English and use the verb 'es'.
nodes.response: When talking about the weather, we use 'hace' to mean 'it is'. We can’t translate weather phrases word for word from English.

nodes.misconception: As pupils first encounter the idea of climate they confuse it with weather.
nodes.response: Keep offering different examples and talk about weather being a snapshot of a moment in time but climate is a long-term trend of weather.

nodes.misconception: Proportional representation was purely a positive step forward because it gave a voice to smaller political parties.
nodes.response: In fact, proportional representation led to fragmentation, with many small parties gaining seats in the Reichstag. This made it difficult to pass laws because no single party had a majority.

nodes.misconception: The NHS was the only feature of Britain's welfare state which supported public health.
nodes.response: The NHS was very important but slum clearance and new house building were also important features of the welfare state which benefitted public health.

nodes.misconception: The British army went into the war confidently, with a large number of troops.
nodes.response: The British army had no more than 700 000 men in August 1914, they would need to use mass recruitment and colonial armies.

nodes.misconception: That the archaeologists used the actual artefacts found in the grave to make the reconstruction of the chariot.
nodes.response: Ensure pupils understand that archaeologists used new materials to make a replica chariot based on the evidence in the grave.

nodes.misconception: The 'Whigs' gained their name because of the fancy wigs and hairstyles that were the fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries.
nodes.response: 'Whigs' has nothing to do with hairstyles, but was instead originally a derogatory term used to describe the 'Country Party', as they were originally known. 'Whig' was a sound Scottish drovers shouted when controlling cattle on the way to market.

nodes.misconception: Students commonly do not provide enough detail from their historic environment in their answers.
nodes.response: Try to back up your analysis of the question with specific facts and details from your historic environment.

nodes.misconception: Children may think that windmills and wind turbines create wind when the sails or blades spin.
nodes.response: Teaching slide explain that windmills and wind turbines harness the energy of the wind to do work for us or to generate electricity.

nodes.misconception: The Windrush generation were illegal migrants.
nodes.response: Those coming from the British Commonwealth were considered citizens.

nodes.misconception: People from the Caribbean travelled to Britain without being invited.
nodes.response: These people were invited to become British citizens by the government in 1948 to help the country recover and lots had contributed in the armed forces during the war too.

nodes.misconception: The witches are presented in one way; any new interpretation supersedes the one before.
nodes.response: The witches are presented as supernatural, women, masculine and genderless. Paragraphs can explore all these; rely on LC2 to draw this out.

nodes.misconception: Some may think that Celtic people and Iron Age people lived in different time periods.
nodes.response: Celtic people lived during the Iron Age.

nodes.misconception: The Qur'an was authored by the Prophet Muhammad.
nodes.response: Most Muslims believe that the Qur'an was revealed to Muhammad and is the word of God (Allah). The Hadith contain sayings of Muhammad collected by his companions.

nodes.misconception: The material an artist uses doesn’t matter as long as the subject or idea is strong.
nodes.response: The choice of materials greatly affects how an artwork looks, feels and communicates meaning. Materials can add texture, symbolism and emotional impact that deepen the viewer’s understanding.

nodes.misconception: Balance means everything must be perfectly symmetrical.
nodes.response: Balance can be symmetrical, but it can also be asymmetrical or radial. Asymmetrical balance uses different elements on each side to create visual stability.

nodes.misconception: Christian charities support Christian individuals and communities.
nodes.response: Christian charities, such as CAFOD, support individuals and communities from many different backgrounds all around the world.

nodes.misconception: Christian Aid only provides short-term emergency help in war zones.
nodes.response: Christian Aid provides both emergency relief and long-term development. Alongside food and shelter, it also helps rebuild homes and schools, supports mental health, and trains local workers to help communities recover after conflict.

nodes.misconception: Alessi is often thought of as a single designer.
nodes.response: Alessi is a group of designers.

nodes.misconception: Tearfund only responds to large scale disasters.
nodes.response: Tearfund responds to both small scale and large scale disasters.

nodes.misconception: Everyone in the Torah or Old Testament always believed in only one god.
nodes.response: Abram's family and the people of Abram's homeland were polytheists, meaning they believed in multiple gods.

nodes.misconception: It is winter at the same time of year all around the world.
nodes.response: It is winter at the North Pole when it is summer at the South Pole.

nodes.misconception: The Pacific ocean is on both sides of the world.
nodes.response: The world is round and spherical in shape like a ball. If we cut it and lay it out flat it will look like there are two Pacific oceans but they are one connected ocean when looking at the Earth in a 3D perspective.

nodes.misconception: Hot deserts are mostly found at the Equator.
nodes.response: Tropical rainforests are found at the Equator. Deserts are mostly found at the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may be used to encountering a detached third person narrator thus expecting most narrators to be trustworthy and reliable.
nodes.response: When a writer chooses to write a story from a characters' perspective, we have to consider that each character  is fallible or unreliable. Thus, we have to re-filter (through our own consciousness) the information we get from a first person narrator.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may not recognise how terms of endearment can be patronising.
nodes.response: Terms of endearment are traditionally used as a sign of affection but they can be used to subdue, belittle or appease someone (depending on the context).

nodes.misconception: That the modern experience of going to the theatre is the same as in Shakespearean times.
nodes.response: The experience was very different - the modern theatre experience is quiet and respectful while the Shakespearean experience was riotous.

nodes.misconception: Theme and variations is the same as theme music.
nodes.response: Theme music is a musical composition which is often written specifically for video games, or films and is usually played at the beginning, end and at some point during the course of the game or film.

nodes.misconception: Final [e] is a long vowel sound in German.
nodes.response: Final [e] is a short [e] sound, as in 'Liebe'. Final [er] is a longer sound, as in 'lieber'.

nodes.misconception: Like in English, a word for 'more' is needed in German when making comparisons like 'more difficult' or 'more interesting'.
nodes.response: German adjectives form comparatives by adding -er; there is no need to include 'more', e.g., more interesting > 'interessanter'; more difficult >'schwieriger'. English does this with 1- and some 2-syllable adjectives, e.g., 'small' > 'smaller'.

nodes.misconception: [qu] sounds the same in English and German.
nodes.response: In German, the SSC [qu] is pronounced 'k' then 'w' (which in German is like the English 'v' sound). Avoid confusion with English - for example, 'Qualität' vs 'quality'. In German, 'kw' appears only in complound words, e.g., 'Trinkwasser'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often do not accept that all objects left in a room for a long time are the same temperature.
nodes.response: Provide opportunities to consolidate the understanding that particles vibrating with more energy transfer some of that energy to particles with less energy through collisions and when bonded together in a solid.

nodes.misconception: Heat is a substance that flows through thermal conductors.
nodes.response: Emphasise that in a solid the particles do not move along the material during thermal conduction and that what we experience as ‘heat’ is particles in an object vibrating against our skin.

nodes.misconception: When interpreting results, pupils may think that the greatest loss of heat has occurred in the cup which has the lowest temperature at the end.
nodes.response: Pupils will be taught they need to consider the change in temperature rather than just using the lowest end temperature to find which cup has led to the greatest heat loss.

nodes.misconception: Children may think that thermal insulators only keep things warm.
nodes.response: Task A specifically addresses this misconception. Children will have opportunities to investigate which cup has the best thermal insulation properties for keeping drinks cold in lesson 5 of this unit.

nodes.misconception: Insulators warm objects up.
nodes.response: Show your class that an insulator keeps an ice cube colder for longer by wrapping one in a conductor (such as aluminium foil) and another in an insulator at the start of the lesson. The ice cube in the conductor will melt first.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may think that thermometers are heat sources.  They may also think that they must touch an object to measure its temperature.
nodes.response: Teaching slides explain how to use a thermometer and show that you can use them to measure ambient temperature.

nodes.misconception: Many pupils are likely to still use the terms current, voltage and resistance interchangeably.
nodes.response: Repeatedly question pupils about each term and challenge them to use each one correctly throughout their explanations, both written and verbal.

nodes.misconception: When German adjectives come before the noun, they don't change their spelling, just like in English, e.g., 'The dog is black'; 'The black dog is over there.'.
nodes.response: In German, when adjectives come after the verb 'sein' (to be) they don't change. However, adjectives in front of a noun add endings do; this is called adjective agreement. There are different endings depending on gender (m, f, nt) and on the article.

nodes.misconception: The terms 'weak verb' and 'strong verb' refer to whether the action is powerful or not.
nodes.response: The term 'weak verb' is used to describe verbs that follow a regular pattern across all tenses. The term 'strong verb' describes verbs that have a stem change in either present or past tenses.

nodes.misconception: It is always a good idea to add external links to your website.
nodes.response: Adding external links to your website can have some implications. For example, the website could be moved and you can then end up with a broken link on your website.

nodes.misconception: Contrasting sections should be totally different to other sections in a composition.
nodes.response: Contrasting sections of music can be derived from some of the same ideas but should have their own recognisable melodic and harmonic ideas.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to generate their own vocabulary or understand the vocabulary given to them.
nodes.response: In LC2, look at the children's expression when they are freeze framing. Then, put the description into a sentence e.g. 'You look terrified.'. The children mirror the facial expression and tone from you and then repeat the sentence.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to generate vocabulary to explain the expressions and movements.
nodes.response: The purpose of learning cycle 1 is to provide the children with vocabulary. Narrate how the children are feeling in their freeze-frames and get them to repeat. For example, you may say 'You look famished.' and the children repeat 'We are famished'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to generate questions.
nodes.response: When you are modelling, model the 'wondering' thought process and discuss what you want to know about, referring to why character's did certain things and how they felt at certain points.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to speak in the fist person imagining they are someone else.
nodes.response: The sentence stems should support. Teachers should ask the question, then say the sentence stem and provide children time to speak to someone to rehearse answers in full sentences. If they don't reply in full sentences, always re-phrase it for them.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may struggle to recall the event of the story to be able to express that part.
nodes.response: When you are re-reading the story at the start of the lesson, model the expression of the characters as you are reading and drip-feed in some vocabulary that you could use.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may say the incorrect pronouns or speak in the incorrect person.
nodes.response: Re-model sentences, emphasising the change of person "**I** lived in a magical, enchanted forest." and get the children to repeat.

nodes.misconception: If the surface is carved too deeply, layers can be glued back on later.
nodes.response: Soap is a soft material, and carving too deeply can cause unintended breakage. It’s important to carve in gradual layers, starting with rough shaping before adding finer details.

nodes.misconception: It is best for lots of attackers to be near the ball so they have more chance of keeping possession.
nodes.response: Overcrowding the ball limits passing options, reduces space and makes it easier for defenders to win possession, so attackers should spread out to keep better control.

nodes.misconception: A third person omniscient narrator must develop each character in the same amount of detail.
nodes.response: Whilst a third person omniscient narrator can develop many characters, they don't need the same amount of space, detail and time in a written piece. You can still have a central character, and minor characters who are more or less important.

nodes.misconception: Art can only be made by one artist, working alone.
nodes.response: Art can be a collaborative process. When artists collaborate, they work together to communicate common meanings or achieve common goals.

nodes.misconception: Craft is only about making functional objects and is less important than Fine Art.
nodes.response: Craft is the creation of objects and artworks requiring both artistry and technical skill. It includes both functional and non-functional items and embraces contributions from all genders and communities.

nodes.misconception: There is no change in word order after time adverbials.
nodes.response: Practise short examples with and without time adverbials, and use cards (or the pupils themselves) to move to demonstrate word order 2 with time adverbials at beginning of sentences.

nodes.misconception: The perfect tense in German is often only translated as 'have done'.
nodes.response: Give clear examples of both translations 'have done' and 'did' with appropriate time adverbials. Emphasise the role of time adverbials in helping to decide on the correct English translation.

nodes.misconception: The German verb for 'use' is needed when saying what used to happen.
nodes.response: 'Used to' in German is communicated by using the adverb 'früher' - 'in the past', 'in former times'. There is no need to include a German verb for 'use'.

nodes.misconception: There has always been a large variety of names that people could be called.
nodes.response: In societies that do not experience a great deal of immigration, the pool of names that people can be called can be limited. This was the case for hundreds of years in England, causing many people to share the same names (e.g. Thomas!).

nodes.misconception: Students think that atmosphere is created purely through the description of a physical setting.
nodes.response: Atmosphere can also be created through characters interacting with one another, as we see in Chapter 11 of 'Jane Eyre'.

nodes.misconception: Caring is only within your family
nodes.response: Caring happens everywhere and with everyone

nodes.misconception: After an opinion verb (e.g., 'denken') and the conjunction 'dass', we use normal subject-verb word order.
nodes.response: To say 'I think that ...' in German, we use the conjunction 'dass', which triggers word order 3 (WO3); e.g., 'Ich denke, dass Rapmusik toll ist.'.

nodes.misconception: Climate change has not impacted tropical rainforests as temperature and rainfall patterns have remained the same.
nodes.response: Climate change has affected tropical rainforests by increasing temperatures, changing rainfall patterns and increasing the frequency of droughts. For example, the Amazon rainforest experienced its worst recorded drought in 2023.

nodes.misconception: Network threats and attacks come only from external hackers or from sources outside a network, while internal users or trusted software pose no risk.
nodes.response: Threats can be internal, like careless employees or malicious insiders, as well as external.

nodes.misconception: Ocean acidification is when water is polluted from human activities on land.
nodes.response: Ocean acidification is when the ocean absorbs extra carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the air, which makes the water more acidic.

nodes.misconception: The main threats to the taiga come from the direct damage done to forests by the logging industry.
nodes.response: While the logging industry does directly damage taiga forests, indirect threats from warming taiga climates are also a major threat to the taiga and taiga biodiversity.

nodes.misconception: That climate change causes global warming, or that climate change and global warming are the same thing.
nodes.response: Global warming is the rise in average temperatures as a result of the greenhouse effect. Climate change is changes to weather patterns (including temperatures and rainfall patterns) as a result of global warming.

nodes.misconception: Pupils may believe using a co-ordinating conjunction always creates a compound sentence.
nodes.response: Using a co-ordinating conjunction only creates a compound sentence if the conjunction is joining main clauses.

nodes.misconception: Pupils *very* easily confuse different types of reactions.
nodes.response: Spend time developing ways to help pupils remember the differences and regularly challenge them to explain why one reaction is the type it is.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think that "because" is a co-ordinating conjunction.
nodes.response: There are three co-ordinating conjunctions that are most frequently used in English. These are "and", "but" and "or".

nodes.misconception: Training at the highest intensity is the best way to see results.
nodes.response: A balanced and accurate approach to training intensity using approximate zones is necessary to optimise fitness, recovery and avoid injury.

nodes.misconception: Training at the highest intensity is the best way to see results.
nodes.response: A balanced and accurate approach to training intensity using approximate zones is necessary to optimise fitness, recovery and avoid injury.

nodes.misconception: When pupils follow through on their throw, they use excessive force which causes them to lose balance, impacting the throw and often causing them to step over the throwing line.
nodes.response: Ensure pupils understand the consequences of stepping over the throwing line - foul throw.

nodes.misconception: A fear of being hit by the ball can cause pupils to flinch, shy away or close their eyes.
nodes.response: Ensure pupils understand that they need to keep their eyes on the ball, focusing on it until it is in their hands.

nodes.misconception: Pupils believe that you throw the shot in the shot put event, similar to how you throw the javelin.
nodes.response: Although 'throw' is often the terminology used when competing in the shot put, pupils should push the shot which starts from under their chin. A throwing action, when using a heavier shot, would likely cause a wrist/elblow/shoulder injury.

nodes.misconception: Pupils grip the javelin tightly in their hand, thinking that this will help them to throw it further, however this can hinder a smooth release and lead to tension in the rest of the arm.
nodes.response: Pupils should place the javelin across their palm with their fingers wrapped around it, but not too tight. Explain to pupils that a more relaxed grip will result in a smoother release and longer throw.

nodes.misconception: Pupils will choose to throw overarm from a distance even if this compromises accuracy.
nodes.response: Accuracy of an overarm throw takes time and practise. Pupils should try exploring both throwing techniques from different distances to judge what is their conformable throwing range.

nodes.misconception: Pupils generate a throwing action using the the arm only.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to use all the body, rather than just the arm when throwing, to help generate power and balance when throwing over a greater distance.

nodes.misconception: Pupils throw with too much force when aiming for a target.
nodes.response: Managing the right amount force of a throw requires practise and trial and error to judge how much force is needed.

nodes.misconception: Pupils believe that throwing requires a lot of strength rather than proper technique.
nodes.response: Ensure that pupils understand that throwing too hard can lead to poor technique and less accuracy when aiming for a target.

nodes.misconception: In a game situation, pupils can panic and rush their throw without aiming or using the correct technique.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to be composed and even when under pressure to throw quickly, ensure pupils understand the importance of throwing accurately with the correct technique.

nodes.misconception: When throwing underarm, pupils often struggle to release the ball so it travels forward towards the target. Pupils may forget to have their hands up ready to catch the the ball.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to develop a smooth arm swing when throwing towards a target and finish with a straight arm pointing in the direction of their target. Remind pupils to adopt the ready position with hands up in front of them when waiting to catch.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often throw the ball with too much power. Pupils step into their throw with the same foot as their throwing arm. Pupils wait for the ball to come to them instead of moving towards it.
nodes.response: Encourage pupils to hold the ball loosely rather than squeezing it tightly. Remind pupils to step in with opposite foot to throwing arm. Pupils should be encouraged to move towards the ball to catch it and make sure the body is underneath the ball.

nodes.misconception: Jewish ethics are concerned with people and not the natural world.
nodes.response: Care for the planet and the environment is found throughout Jewish teaching and has deep roots.

nodes.misconception: All timbers are sustainable.
nodes.response: Timber can be a sustainable material if sourced from a Forest Stewardship Council certified supplier. FSC forests are managed to strict environmental, social, and ecological standards.

nodes.misconception: Softwoods are soft and light, hardwoods are hard and heavy.
nodes.response: The terms softwood and hardwood don’t refer to how soft or hard the wood is. They classify trees based on their seed type. Many softwoods are softer than hardwoods but it's not a strict rule. Balsa is a hardwood, but it’s one of the softest woods.

nodes.misconception: Toms are only used in fills. Use of the snare/claps/clicks will automatically be a backbeat.
nodes.response: Toms can be used in the main groove just less commonly than the kick/snare. For a backbeat the snare/claps have to play on beats 2 and 4.

nodes.misconception: It is impossible to memorise the timbre of all of the different instruments around the world.
nodes.response: Yes, it would be impossible. However, learning to identify some of the key instruments is valuable - these are often heard in styles across different cultures, so learning the sound of the most common is important as a well-rounded musician.

nodes.misconception: The only translation of 'que' is 'that'.
nodes.response: In Spanish, 'que' can mean different things depending on the context in which it's used. For example, it can mean 'who' or 'that' as a relative pronoun, or 'than' within a comparative structure.

nodes.misconception: Pupils think punctuality is merely about turning up to lessons on time.
nodes.response: Punctuality is linked to arrival time, but is also about completing tasks on time and being respectful for the time of others. This is achieved by being organised, fulfilling the task and being dependable.

nodes.misconception: Gantt charts are used to plan out the whole design project.
nodes.response: Gantt charts can be used as a tool to plan out the whole design project. However it can be beneficial to use Gantt charts for the individual phases within the project, like the manufacturing stage. This can improve efficiency at crucial stages.

nodes.misconception: I do not need to plan for a debate.
nodes.response: To participate effectively in debate you will need to have clear arguments and rebuttals, that are backed up with evidence. Planning will ensure you can do this confidently.

nodes.misconception: When referring to who or what somebody is in French, we must use 'il est' or 'elle est', like in English: she is my cousin.
nodes.response: When referring to who or what somebody is in French, we can use 'il est' or 'elle est', like in English. We can also use 'c'est': c'est ma cousine - she is my cousin.

nodes.misconception: Use the same word order as English when using indirect object pronouns.
nodes.response: In German, the indirect object pronoun comes straight after the verb, not at the end of the sentence. For example, 'Musik ist mir wichtig.' - 'Music is important to me.'.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often believe that any small colour change signals the end point, leading to inaccurate titrations.
nodes.response: Emphasise the importance of adding the titrant drop by drop near the end point and ensure pupils understand that the end point is reached only when the colour change is persistent.

nodes.misconception: Pupils use all of their titration results to calculate an average volume used during titration. Pupils also tend to miss steps in this multistep process.
nodes.response: Stress the need to use concordant results when calculating an average volume for neutralising a solution via titration. Use a calculation grid to help keep each calculation step clearly organised.

nodes.misconception: Pupils use all of their titration results to calculate an average volume used during titration. Pupils also tend to miss steps in this multi-step process.
nodes.response: Stress the need to use concordant results when calculating an average volume for neutralising a solution via titration. Use a calculation grid to help keep each calculation step clearly organised.

nodes.misconception: Pupils often overshoot the end point, especially on their first attempt at a titration.
nodes.response: Pupils will need to work on their dexterity, often with a partner, to ensure the flow of titrant is slow enough from the burette, and that their swirling technique allows ample mixing of the solutions.

nodes.misconception: Living standards and quality of life are the same.
nodes.response: Living standards are about the the level of necessities and comforts of daily life that is available to and affordable by a person.

nodes.misconception: TNCs have helped Indonesia to develop its own vehicle manufacturing companies.
nodes.response: While TNCs have been important in developing vehicle manufacturing in Indonesia, the vehicles they make are not Indonesian brands and the profits from selling them in Indonesia or in export markets go to the TNCs and not to Indonesian companies.

nodes.misconception: Confusion between 'il a' and 'il est' as 'il est' is pronounced similarly to the English 'a'.
nodes.response: 'Il a' and 'il est' are pronounced differently and have different meanings: 'il a' is he has and 'il est' is he is.

nodes.misconception: The perfect tense is made up of one part like it is in English.
nodes.response: You must have both parts of the perfect tense; the present tense of 'avoir' and a past participle. Regular past participles end in é.

nodes.misconception: There is no difference in French between the present and perfect tense forms 'I do' and 'I did', 'I say' and 'I said', because they sound the same.
nodes.response: The spellings of the past participles 'fait' and 'dit' are different to the first person (I) present tense but sound the same because of silent final consonants. Another difference is using 'j'ai' before past participles to say 'I did'.

nodes.misconception: There is one way to say 'we are' in Spanish.
nodes.response: There are two ways to say 'we are' in Spanish. Estamos is used to say 'we are' for location and temporary state. Somos is used to say 'we are' for general traits.

nodes.misconception: There is only one way to say 'they are' in Spanish.
nodes.response: In Spanish, there are two verbs for 'to be, being': estar and ser. To say 'they are'with estar, we use 'están' for location and temporary states. To say 'they are' with ser, we use 'son' for general traits.

nodes.misconception: There is only one verb for 'to be, being' in Spanish.
nodes.response: There are two verbs for to be in Spanish: 'estar' for location and temporary states and 'ser' for general traits.

nodes.misconception: Role-play and conversation answers should be kept brief.
